translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 158

sentences.zh: 【梁紀十四】　起著雍敦牂，盡閼逢困敦，凡七年。

translations.literal: [Liang Records 14] From Zhuoyong Dunzhang through Quefeng Kundun; seven years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Liang Records 14] The span runs from Zhuoyong Dunzhang through Quefeng Kundun—seven years in all.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝十四大同四年（

translations.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Wu, year 14 of the Datong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, fourteenth year of Datong (

sentences.zh: 戊午，公元五三八年）

translations.literal: wuwu, 538 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wuwu, AD 538)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of xinyou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of xinyou, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 東魏碭郡獲巨像，送鄴。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei's Dang commandery obtained a colossal image and sent it to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei's Dang commandery unearthed a colossal image and sent it to Ye.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，大赦，改元元象。

translations.literal: On dingmao, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Yuanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the court proclaimed a general amnesty and adopted the era name Yuanxiang.

sentences.zh: 二月，己亥，上耕藉田。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jihai, the emperor plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jihai, the Liang emperor performed the ceremonial plowing of the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 東魏大都督善無賀拔仁攻魏南汾州，刺史韋子粲降之，丞相泰滅子粲之族。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Grand Commander Heluoba Ren of Shanwu attacked Western Wei's Nanfen province; Inspector Wei Zican surrendered; Chancellor Yuwen Tai exterminated Zican's clan.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei's Grand Commander Heluoba Ren of Shanwu attacked Western Wei's Nanfen province. Inspector Wei Zican surrendered, and Chancellor Yuwen Tai wiped out Zican's clan.

sentences.zh: 東魏大行台侯景等治兵於虎牢，將復河南諸州，魏梁回、韋孝寬、趙繼宗皆棄城西歸。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Grand Commissioner Hou Jing and others mustered troops at Hulao to recover the Henan provinces; Western Wei's Liang Hui, Wei Xiaokuan, and Zhao Jizong all abandoned their cities and withdrew west.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei Grand Commissioner Hou Jing and others mustered troops at Hulao to retake the Henan provinces. Liang Hui, Wei Xiaokuan, and Zhao Jizong of Western Wei abandoned their posts and withdrew west.

sentences.zh: 侯景攻廣州，數旬，未拔，聞魏救兵將至，集諸將議之，行洛州事盧勇請進觀形勢。

translations.literal: Hou Jing attacked Guang province; for many weeks he could not take it. Hearing that Western Wei relief was coming, he gathered his generals to discuss the matter; Lu Yong, acting governor of Luozhou, asked to advance and reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing besieged Guang province for weeks without success. When word came that Western Wei relief was near, he called his generals to council; Lu Yong, acting governor of Luozhou, asked leave to ride ahead and scout.

sentences.zh: 乃帥百騎至大隗山，遇魏師。

translations.literal: He then led a hundred horsemen to Mount Dawei and encountered the Western Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: He led a hundred horsemen to Mount Dawei and ran into the Western Wei army.

sentences.zh: 日已暮，勇多置幡旗於樹顛；

translations.literal: The sun had already set; Yong planted many banners atop the trees;
translations.idiomatic: The sun was down; Yong planted banners thick on the treetops;

sentences.zh: 夜，分騎為十隊，鳴角直前，擒魏儀同三司程華，斬儀同三司王征蠻而還。

translations.literal: at night he divided his riders into ten squads, sounded horns, and charged straight ahead, capturing Western Wei Yitong Sansi Cheng Hua and beheading Yitong Sansi Wang Zhenman before returning.
translations.idiomatic: that night he split his riders into ten squads, sounded horns, and charged straight in—capturing Western Wei's Yitong Sansi Cheng Hua, beheading Yitong Sansi Wang Zhenman, and riding back.

sentences.zh: 廣州守將駱超遂以城降東魏，丞相歡以勇行廣州事。

translations.literal: Guangzhou's defender Luo Chao then surrendered the city to Eastern Wei; Chancellor Gao Huan put Yong in charge of Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou's commander Luo Chao surrendered to Eastern Wei; Gao Huan put Yong in charge of the province.

sentences.zh: 勇，辯之從弟也。

translations.literal: Yong was a cousin of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was a cousin of Bian.

sentences.zh: 於是南汾、穎、豫、廣四州復入東魏。

translations.literal: Nanfen, Ying, Yu, and Guang provinces thus returned to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Nanfen, Ying, Yu, and Guang provinces thus returned to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 初，柔然頭兵可汗始得返國，事魏盡禮。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Rouran khan Toubing had regained his realm, he served Western Wei with full courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran khan Toubing first regained his realm, he had served Western Wei with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 及永安以後，雄據北方，禮漸驕倨，雖信使不絕，不復稱臣。

translations.literal: After the Yongan era he held the north in strength; his courtesy grew arrogant, and though envoys still passed between them, he no longer styled himself a subject.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongan era he dominated the north; his courtesy turned arrogant, and though envoys still passed, he no longer called himself a subject.

sentences.zh: 頭兵嘗至洛陽，心慕中國，乃置侍中、黃門等官；

translations.literal: Toubing had once come to Luoyang, admired China, and set up offices such as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Yellow Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Toubing had once visited Luoyang, admired China, and created offices such as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Yellow Gate;

sentences.zh: 後得魏汝陽王典簽淳於覃，親寵任事，以為秘書監，使典文翰。

translations.literal: later he obtained Chunyu Tan, clerk to Western Wei's Prince of Ruyang, favored him, made him Secretary Supervisor, and had him handle documents.
translations.idiomatic: later he won over Chunyu Tan, a clerk to Western Wei's Prince of Ruyang, favored him, made him Secretary Supervisor, and put him in charge of documents.

sentences.zh: 及兩魏分裂，頭兵轉不遜，數為邊患。

translations.literal: When the two Weis split, Toubing grew more insolent and repeatedly raided the border.
translations.idiomatic: After the two Weis split, Toubing grew more insolent and raided the frontier again and again.

sentences.zh: 魏丞相泰以新都關中，方有事山東，欲結婚以撫之，以舍人元翌女為化政公主，妻頭兵弟塔寒。

translations.literal: Western Wei Chancellor Yuwen Tai, having moved the capital to Guanzhong and being occupied with Shandong, wished to pacify him by marriage: he made Gentleman Yuan Yi's daughter Princess of Huazheng and gave her to Toubing's brother Tahan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai, with the capital now in Guanzhong and his hands full in Shandong, sought to pacify him by marriage—making Gentleman Yuan Yi's daughter Princess of Huazheng and giving her to Toubing's brother Tahan.

sentences.zh: 又言於魏主，請廢乙弗後，納頭兵之女。

translations.literal: He also urged the Western Wei sovereign to depose Empress Yifu and take Toubing's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the Western Wei emperor to depose Empress Yifu and take Toubing's daughter.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以乙弗後為尼，使扶風王孚迎頭兵女為後。

translations.literal: On jiachen, Empress Yifu was made a nun, and the Prince of Fufeng, Fu, was sent to welcome Toubing's daughter as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Empress Yifu was tonsured, and the Prince of Fufeng, Fu, was sent to welcome Toubing's daughter as empress.

sentences.zh: 頭兵遂留東魏使者元整，不報其使。

translations.literal: Toubing then detained Eastern Wei's envoy Yuan Zheng and gave no reply to their mission.
translations.idiomatic: Toubing then detained Eastern Wei's envoy Yuan Zheng and sent no answer to their mission.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛酉，東魏丞相歡以沙苑之敗，請解大丞相，詔許之；

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinyou, Eastern Wei Chancellor Gao Huan, because of the defeat at Shaya, asked to resign as Grand Chancellor; the edict permitted it;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinyou, Gao Huan asked to resign as Grand Chancellor after the defeat at Shaya; the court assented;

sentences.zh: 頃之，復故。

translations.literal: shortly afterward he was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: shortly afterward he was restored as before.

sentences.zh: 柔然送悼後於魏，車七百乘、馬萬匹、駝二千頭。

translations.literal: The Rouran sent their empress to Western Wei with seven hundred carriages, ten thousand horses, and two thousand camels.
translations.idiomatic: The Rouran sent their empress to Western Wei with seven hundred carriages, ten thousand horses, and two thousand camels.

sentences.zh: 至黑鹽池，遇魏所遣鹵簿儀衛。

translations.literal: At Black Salt Pool she met the honor guard Western Wei had dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: At Black Salt Pool she met the honor guard Western Wei had dispatched.

sentences.zh: 柔然營幕，戶席皆東向，扶風王孚請正南面，後曰：「我未見魏主，固柔然女也。

translations.literal: In the Rouran camp every tent and seat faced east; the Prince of Fufeng, Fu, asked the empress to face due south; the empress said, "I have not yet seen the Western Wei sovereign—I am still a Rouran woman.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rouran camp every tent and seat faced east; the Prince of Fufeng, Fu, asked the empress to face due south. She said, "I have not yet seen the Western Wei emperor—I am still a Rouran woman.

sentences.zh: 魏仗南面，我自東向。

translations.literal: Western Wei's escort faces south; I face east myself.
translations.idiomatic: Let Western Wei's escort face south; I face east."

sentences.zh: 」丙子，立皇后郁久閭氏。

translations.literal: " On bingzi, Empress Yujiu Lü was installed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Empress Yujiu Lü was installed.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingchou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the court proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 以王盟為司徒。

translations.literal: Wang Meng was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng was made Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 丞相泰朝於長安，還屯華州。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yuwen Tai attended court at Chang'an, then returned to camp at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai attended court at Chang'an, then returned to camp at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚寅，東魏高歡朝於鄴；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on gengyin, Eastern Wei's Gao Huan attended court at Ye;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengyin, Gao Huan of Eastern Wei attended court at Ye;

sentences.zh: 壬辰，還晉陽。

translations.literal: on renchen he returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: on renchen he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲戌，東魏遣兼散騎常侍鄭伯猷來聘。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiaxu, Eastern Wei sent Acting Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Zheng Boyou on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiaxu, Eastern Wei sent Acting Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Zheng Boyou on a friendly mission.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，東魏荊州刺史王則寇淮南。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Eastern Wei's Jing province inspector Wang Ze raided Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Eastern Wei's Jing province inspector Wang Ze raided Huainan.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，詔以東冶徒李胤之得如來捨利，大赦。

translations.literal: On guihai, an edict proclaimed a general amnesty because the eastern-smelting convict Li Yinzhi had obtained a Buddha relic.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai an edict proclaimed a general amnesty because the eastern-smelting convict Li Yinzhi had obtained a Buddha relic.

sentences.zh: 東魏侯景、高敖曹等圍魏獨孤信於金墉，太師歡帥大軍繼之；

translations.literal: Eastern Wei's Hou Jing, Gao Aocao, and others besieged Western Wei's Dugu Xin at Jinyong; Grand Mentor Gao Huan led a great army in support;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei's Hou Jing, Gao Aocao, and others besieged Dugu Xin at Jinyong; Grand Mentor Gao Huan followed with a great army;

sentences.zh: 景悉燒洛陽內外官寺民居，存者什二三。

translations.literal: Jing burned every official temple and dwelling inside and outside Luoyang; barely one or two in ten survived.
translations.idiomatic: Jing burned every official temple and dwelling inside and outside Luoyang; barely one or two in ten survived.

sentences.zh: 魏主將如洛陽拜園陵，會信等告急，遂與丞相泰俱東，命尚書左僕射周惠達輔太子欽守長安，開府儀同三司李弼、車騎大將軍達奚武帥千騎為前驅。

translations.literal: The Western Wei emperor was about to go to Luoyang to worship the imperial tombs when Xin's urgent report arrived; he went east with Chancellor Yuwen Tai, left Left Vice Director Zhou Huida to assist Crown Prince Qin at Chang'an, and sent Kaifu Yitong Sansi Li Bi and Grand General of Cavalry Daxi Wu ahead with a thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei emperor was about to visit the Luoyang tombs when Xin's urgent report arrived. He marched east with Yuwen Tai, left Zhou Huida to assist Crown Prince Qin at Chang'an, and sent Li Bi and Daxi Wu ahead with a thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚寅，丞相泰至谷城，侯景等欲整陳以待其至，儀同三司太安莫多婁貸文請帥所部擊其前鋒，景等固止之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengyin, Chancellor Yuwen Tai reached Gucheng; Hou Jing and the others meant to form battle lines and await him; Yitong Sansi Mo Duo Lou Daiwen asked to lead his division against the vanguard, but Jing and the rest firmly stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengyin, Yuwen Tai reached Gucheng. Hou Jing and the others meant to form battle lines and await him; Yitong Sansi Mo Duo Lou Daiwen asked to lead his division against the vanguard, but Jing and the rest overruled him.

sentences.zh: 貸文勇而專，不受命，與可朱渾道元以千騎前進。

translations.literal: Daiwen was brave and willful; he disobeyed orders and advanced with Kezhunhun Daoyuan at the head of a thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Daiwen was brave and willful; he disobeyed orders and rode forward with Kezhunhun Daoyuan at the head of a thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 夜，遇李弼、達奚武於孝水。

translations.literal: By night they met Li Bi and Daxi Wu at the Xiao River.
translations.idiomatic: By night they met Li Bi and Daxi Wu at the Xiao River.

sentences.zh: 弼命軍士鼓噪，曳柴揚塵，貸文走，弼追斬之，道元單騎獲免，悉俘其眾送恆農。

translations.literal: Bi ordered his men to shout and beat drums, drag brushwood, and raise dust; Daiwen fled; Bi pursued and beheaded him; Daoyuan escaped alone on horseback; Bi captured the whole force and sent it to Hengnong.
translations.idiomatic: Bi ordered his men to shout and drum, drag brushwood, and raise dust. Daiwen fled; Bi ran him down and beheaded him. Daoyuan escaped alone; Bi took the whole force prisoner and sent them to Hengnong.

sentences.zh: 泰進軍瀍東，侯景等夜解圍去。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai advanced east of the Chan River; Hou Jing and the others lifted the siege by night and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai advanced east of the Chan; Hou Jing and the others lifted the siege by night and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，泰帥輕騎追景至河上，景為陳，北據河橋，南屬邙山，與泰合戰。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Yuwen Tai led light cavalry in pursuit of Jing to the river; Jing formed his line with the river bridge to the north and the Mang hills to the south, and joined battle with Yuwen Tai.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Yuwen Tai led light cavalry after Jing to the river. Jing formed his line with the river bridge to the north and the Mang hills to the south, and closed with Yuwen Tai.

sentences.zh: 泰馬中流矢驚逸，遂失所之。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai's horse was struck by an arrow, panicked, and bolted; he lost his way.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai's horse took an arrow, panicked, and bolted; he was separated from his men.

sentences.zh: 泰墜地，東魏兵追及之，左右皆散，都督李穆下馬，以策抶泰背罵曰：「籠東軍士！

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai fell; Eastern Wei soldiers caught up; his attendants scattered; Commander Li Mu dismounted, whipped Yuwen Tai's back with his riding crop, and shouted, "Soldiers of Longdong!
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai fell. Eastern Wei soldiers closed in; his attendants scattered. Commander Li Mu dismounted, whipped Yuwen Tai's back with his crop, and roared, "Soldiers of Longdong!

sentences.zh: 爾曹主何在，而獨留此？

translations.literal: Where is your master, that you linger here alone?
translations.idiomatic: Where is your master, that you linger here alone?

sentences.zh: 」追者不疑其貴人，捨之而過。

translations.literal: " The pursuers did not suspect he was a man of rank and let him pass.
translations.idiomatic: " The pursuers took him for a common soldier and let him pass.

sentences.zh: 穆以馬授泰，與之俱逸。

translations.literal: Mu gave Yuwen Tai his horse, and both escaped together.
translations.idiomatic: Mu gave Yuwen Tai his horse, and both escaped together.

sentences.zh: 魏兵復振，擊東魏兵，大破之，東魏兵北走。

translations.literal: The Western Wei army rallied, struck the Eastern Wei army, and routed them; the Eastern Wei army fled north.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei army rallied, struck the Eastern Wei army, and broke them; the Eastern Wei men fled north.

sentences.zh: 京兆忠武公高敖曹，意輕泰，建旗蓋以陵陳，魏人盡銳攻之，一軍皆沒，敖曹單騎走投河陽南城。

translations.literal: Gao Aocao, Duke of Loyal Martial of Jingzhao, despised Yuwen Tai and raised banners and canopy to dominate the line; the Western Wei threw every elite at him, his whole command was destroyed, and Aocao fled alone toward the south gate of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Aocao, Duke of Loyal Martial of Jingzhao, despised Yuwen Tai and raised banners and canopy to lord over the line. Western Wei threw every elite at him until his whole command was gone; Aocao fled alone toward Heyang's south gate.

sentences.zh: 守將北豫州刺史高永樂，歡之從祖兄子也，與敖曹有怨，閉門不受。

translations.literal: The garrison commander, Northern Yu province inspector Gao Yongle—a cousin's son of Gao Huan—bore a grudge against Aocao and shut the gate against him.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander, Northern Yu inspector Gao Yongle—a cousin's son of Gao Huan—bore a grudge against Aocao and shut the gate against him.

sentences.zh: 敖曹仰呼求繩，不得，拔刀穿闔未徹而追兵至。

translations.literal: Aocao shouted upward for a rope; none came; he drew his sword to pierce the gate before it gave way, and the pursuers arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Aocao shouted up for a rope; none came. He drew his sword to pierce the gate before it gave way, and the pursuers were upon him.

sentences.zh: 敖曹伏橋下，追者見其從奴持金帶，問敖曹所在，奴指示之。

translations.literal: Aocao hid under the bridge; pursuers saw his attendant holding a gold belt, asked where Aocao was, and the slave pointed him out.
translations.idiomatic: Aocao hid under the bridge. Pursuers saw his attendant with a gold belt, asked where Aocao was, and the slave pointed him out.

sentences.zh: 敖曹知不免，奮頭曰：「來！

translations.literal: Knowing he could not escape, Aocao raised his head and said, "Come!
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not escape, Aocao raised his head and said, "Come!

sentences.zh: 與汝開國公。

translations.literal: I'll make you a Duke Who Founded a State.
translations.idiomatic: I'll make you a Duke Who Founded a State."

sentences.zh: 」追者斬其首去。

translations.literal: " The pursuers cut off his head and left.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers cut off his head and left.

sentences.zh: 高歡聞之，如喪肝膽，杖高永樂二百，贈敖曹太師、大司馬、太尉。

translations.literal: Gao Huan heard of it as if he had lost liver and gall; he had Gao Yongle beaten two hundred strokes and posthumously honored Aocao as Grand Tutor, Grand Marshal, and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan heard of it as if he had lost his vitals; he had Gao Yongle beaten two hundred strokes and posthumously honored Aocao as Grand Tutor, Grand Marshal, and Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 泰賞殺敖曹者布絹萬段，歲歲稍與之，比及周亡，猶未能足。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai rewarded Aocao's killer with ten thousand bolts of silk, giving a little more each year; by the fall of Zhou the debt was still not fully paid.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai rewarded Aocao's killer with ten thousand bolts of silk, adding a little more each year; by the fall of Zhou the debt was still not fully paid.

sentences.zh: 魏又殺東魏西兗州刺史宋顯等，虜甲士萬五千人，赴河死者以萬數。

translations.literal: Western Wei also killed Eastern Wei's western Yan province inspector Song Xian and others, took fifteen thousand armored soldiers prisoner, and tens of thousands drowned in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei also killed Eastern Wei's western Yan inspector Song Xian and others, took fifteen thousand armored men prisoner, and tens of thousands drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 初，歡以-{万俟}-普尊老，特禮之，嘗親扶上馬。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Moqi Puzun was old, Gao Huan had shown him special courtesy and once helped him mount his horse in person.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Moqi Puzun was old, Gao Huan had shown him special courtesy and once helped him mount in person.

sentences.zh: 其子洛免冠稽首曰：「願出死力以報深恩。

translations.literal: His son Luo bared his head and kowtowed, saying, "I wish to give my life's strength to repay your deep grace.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luo bared his head and kowtowed, saying, "I wish to give my life's strength to repay your deep grace."

sentences.zh: 」及邙山之戰，諸軍北度橋，洛獨勒兵不動，謂魏人曰：「-{万俟}-受洛干在此，能來可來也！

translations.literal: " At the battle of Mangshan, as the armies crossed the bridge north, Luo alone held his troops motionless and called to the Western Wei men, "Moqi Shouluogan is here—if you can come, come!
translations.idiomatic: At Mangshan, as the armies crossed the bridge north, Luo alone held his troops and called to Western Wei, "Moqi Shouluogan is here—if you dare, come!

sentences.zh: 」魏人畏之而去，歡名其所營地為回洛。

translations.literal: " The Western Wei men feared him and withdrew; Gao Huan named his camp ground Huiluo.
translations.idiomatic: " Western Wei feared him and withdrew; Gao Huan named his camp ground Huiluo.

sentences.zh: 是日，東、西魏置陳既大，首尾懸遠，從旦至未，戰數十合，氛霧四塞，莫能相知。

translations.literal: That day the Eastern and Western Wei battle lines were vast, head and tail far apart; from dawn to the wei hour they fought dozens of engagements; mist filled every quarter and neither side could tell friend from foe.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Eastern and Western Wei lines were vast, head and tail far apart; from dawn to the wei hour they fought dozens of rounds; mist filled every quarter and neither side could tell friend from foe.

sentences.zh: 魏獨孤信、李遠居右，趙貴、怡峰居左，戰並不利；

translations.literal: Western Wei's Dugu Xin and Li Yuan held the right; Zhao Gui and Yi Feng the left—both wings fought badly;
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin and Li Yuan held Western Wei's right; Zhao Gui and Yi Feng the left—both wings were beaten;

sentences.zh: 又未知魏主及丞相泰所在，皆棄其卒先歸。

translations.literal: they also did not know where the Western Wei emperor and Chancellor Yuwen Tai were, and all abandoned their troops and fled first.
translations.idiomatic: they also did not know where the Western Wei emperor and Yuwen Tai were, and all abandoned their men and fled first.

sentences.zh: 開府儀同三司李虎、念賢等為後軍，見信等退，即與俱去。

translations.literal: Kaifu Yitong Sansi Li Hu, Nian Xian, and others formed the rear; seeing Xin and the rest retreat, they withdrew with them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hu, Nian Xian, and others formed the rear; seeing Xin and the rest retreat, they withdrew with them.

sentences.zh: 泰由是燒營而歸，留儀同三司長孫子彥守金墉。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai therefore burned his camp and withdrew, leaving Yitong Sansi Changsun Ziyan to hold Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai burned his camp and withdrew, leaving Changsun Ziyan to hold Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 王思政下馬，舉長槊左右橫擊，一舉輒踣數人。

translations.literal: Wang Sizheng dismounted, raised his long spear, and struck left and right across the line; each blow knocked down several men.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng dismounted, raised his long spear, and struck left and right; each sweep knocked down several men.

sentences.zh: 陷陳既深，從者盡死，思政被重創，悶絕。

translations.literal: He had driven deep into the enemy line; his followers were all dead; Sizheng took grave wounds and fainted.
translations.idiomatic: He had driven deep into the enemy line; his followers were all dead; Sizheng took grave wounds and fainted.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，敵亦收兵。

translations.literal: At sunset the enemy also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At sunset the enemy also withdrew.

sentences.zh: 思政每戰常著破衣弊甲，敵不知其將帥，故得免。

translations.literal: Sizheng always fought in worn clothes and poor armor, so the enemy did not know he was a general and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng always fought in worn clothes and poor armor, so the enemy did not know he was a general and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 帳下督雷五安於戰處哭求思政，會其已蘇，割衣裹創，扶思政上馬。

translations.literal: His aide Lei Wu'an wept and searched for Sizheng on the field; finding him already awake, he cut cloth to bind his wounds and helped Sizheng mount.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Lei Wu'an wept and searched for Sizheng on the field; finding him already awake, he cut cloth to bind his wounds and helped him mount.

sentences.zh: 夜久，始得還營。

translations.literal: Late into the night he finally returned to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Late into the night he finally returned to camp.

sentences.zh: 平東將軍蔡祐下馬步鬥，左右勸乘馬以備倉猝，祐怒曰：「丞相愛我如子，今日豈惜生乎！

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the East Cai You dismounted to fight on foot; his attendants urged him to mount against sudden danger; You angrily said, "The chancellor loves me like a son—would I spare my life today!
translations.idiomatic: Cai You, General Who Pacifies the East, dismounted to fight on foot. His men urged him to mount against sudden danger; You snapped, "The chancellor loves me like a son—would I spare my life today!

sentences.zh: 」帥左右十餘人合聲大呼，擊東魏兵，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: " He led a dozen men in a single shout, struck the Eastern Wei army, and killed and wounded many.
translations.idiomatic: " He led a dozen men in one shout, struck the Eastern Wei line, and killed and wounded many.

sentences.zh: 東魏人圍之十餘重，祐彎弓持滿，四面拒之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei surrounded him more than ten deep; You drew his bow full and held them off on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei surrounded him more than ten deep; You drew his bow full and held them off on every side.

sentences.zh: 東魏人募厚甲長刀者直進取之，去祐可三十步，左右勸射之，祐曰：「吾曹之命，在此一矢，豈可虛發！

translations.literal: Eastern Wei recruited men in heavy armor with long blades to advance straight on him; they were thirty paces away when his men urged him to shoot; You said, "Our lives hang on this one arrow—how can I loose it in vain!
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent heavy-armored men with long blades straight at him. At thirty paces his men urged him to shoot; You said, "Our lives hang on this one arrow—how can I waste it!

sentences.zh: 」將至十步，祐乃射之，應弦而倒，東魏兵稍卻，祐徐引還。

translations.literal: " When they were ten paces away, You shot; the man fell at the bowstring's sound; the Eastern Wei troops fell back slightly, and You withdrew at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: " At ten paces he shot; the man fell at the bowstring's sound; Eastern Wei fell back a little, and You withdrew at leisure.

sentences.zh: 魏主至恆農，守將已棄城走，所虜降卒在恆農者相與閉門拒守，丞相泰攻拔之，誅其魁首數百人。

translations.literal: The Western Wei emperor reached Hengnong; the garrison commander had already abandoned the city and fled; captured Eastern Wei troops at Hengnong together shut the gates to resist; Chancellor Yuwen Tai stormed the city, took it, and executed several hundred ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei emperor reached Hengnong; the garrison commander had already fled. Captured Eastern Wei troops there shut the gates to resist; Yuwen Tai stormed the city, took it, and executed several hundred ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 蔡祐追及泰於恆農，夜，見泰，泰曰：「承先，爾來，吾無憂矣。

translations.literal: Cai You caught up with Yuwen Tai at Hengnong; by night he saw Tai; Tai said, "Chenxian, you have come—I have no more worries.
translations.idiomatic: Cai You caught Yuwen Tai at Hengnong. That night he came before him; Tai said, "Chenxian, you have come—I have no more worries."

sentences.zh: 」泰驚不得寢，枕祐股，然後安。

translations.literal: " Tai was too shaken to sleep until he rested his head on You's thigh; only then was he at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was too shaken to sleep until he rested his head on You's thigh; only then could he rest.

sentences.zh: 祐每從泰戰，常為士卒先。

translations.literal: Whenever You followed Yuwen Tai into battle, he always led the soldiers first.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever You followed Yuwen Tai into battle, he always led the soldiers first.

sentences.zh: 戰還，諸將皆爭功，祐終無所言。

translations.literal: After battle the generals all contended for merit; You never spoke.
translations.idiomatic: After battle the generals all contended for merit; You never spoke.

sentences.zh: 泰每歎曰：「承先口不言勳，我當代其論敘。

translations.literal: Yuwen Tai often sighed, "Chenxian's mouth never speaks of merit—I must speak his deeds for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai often sighed, "Chenxian never speaks of his merit—I must speak it for him."

sentences.zh: 」泰留王思政鎮恆農，除侍中、東道行台。

translations.literal: " Yuwen Tai left Wang Sizheng to garrison Hengnong and appointed him Attendant-in-Ordinary and Eastern Route Grand Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai left Wang Sizheng to garrison Hengnong and made him Attendant-in-Ordinary and Eastern Route Grand Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 魏之東伐也，關中留守兵少，前後所虜東魏士卒散在民間，聞魏兵敗，謀作亂。

translations.literal: When Western Wei marched east, few troops remained in Guanzhong; Eastern Wei soldiers captured earlier and scattered among the people heard that Western Wei had been defeated and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Wei marched east, few troops remained in Guanzhong; Eastern Wei prisoners scattered among the people heard Western Wei had been beaten and plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 李虎等至長安，計無所出，與太尉王盟、僕射周惠達等奉太子欽出屯渭北。

translations.literal: Li Hu and the others reached Chang'an with no plan; with Grand Commandant Wang Meng, Vice Director Zhou Huida, and the rest they escorted Crown Prince Qin to camp north of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hu and the others reached Chang'an at a loss; with Grand Commandant Wang Meng, Vice Director Zhou Huida, and the rest they escorted Crown Prince Qin to camp north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 百姓互相剽掠，關中大擾。

translations.literal: The common people plundered one another; Guanzhong was in great turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The people plundered one another; Guanzhong was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 於是沙苑所虜東魏都督趙青雀、雍州民於伏德等遂反，青雀據長安子城，伏德保咸陽，與咸陽太守慕容思慶各收降卒以拒還兵。

translations.literal: Then Zhao Qingque, an Eastern Wei commander captured at Shaya, and Yu Fude, a man of Yong province, rebelled; Qingque held Chang'an's inner city, Fude held Xianyang, and with Xianyang governor Murong Siqing each gathered surrendered troops to resist the returning army.
translations.idiomatic: Then Zhao Qingque, an Eastern Wei commander taken at Shaya, and Yu Fude of Yong province rebelled. Qingque held Chang'an's inner city, Fude held Xianyang, and with Xianyang governor Murong Siqing they gathered surrendered troops to block the returning army.

sentences.zh: 長安大城民相帥以拒青雀，日與之戰。

translations.literal: The people of Chang'an's outer city together led resistance to Qingque and fought him daily.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chang'an's outer city banded together to resist Qingque and fought him daily.

sentences.zh: 大都督侯莫陳順擊賊，屢破之，賊不敢出。

translations.literal: Grand Commander Houmochen Shun attacked the rebels, repeatedly defeated them, and the rebels dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander Houmochen Shun attacked the rebels, beat them again and again, and they dared not come out.

sentences.zh: 順，崇之兄也。

translations.literal: Shun was the elder brother of Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was the elder brother of Chong.

sentences.zh: 扶風公王羆鎮河東，大開城門，悉召軍士謂曰：「今聞大軍失利，青雀作亂，諸人莫有固志。

translations.literal: Duke of Fufeng Wang Pi garrisoned Hedong, opened the city gates wide, and summoned all the soldiers, saying, "Word has come that the great army was defeated and Qingque has risen in revolt—none of you should lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi, Duke of Fufeng, held Hedong. He threw open the gates, called every soldier, and said, "Word has come that the great army was beaten and Qingque has risen—none of you should lose heart.

sentences.zh: 王羆受委於此，以死報恩。

translations.literal: Wang Pi has been entrusted here and will repay grace with his death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi has been entrusted here and will repay that grace with his life.

sentences.zh: 有能同心者可共固守；

translations.literal: Whoever can stand together may hold the city with me;
translations.idiomatic: Whoever will stand with me, hold the city;

sentences.zh: 必恐城陷，任自出城。

translations.literal: whoever fears the city will fall may leave whenever he wishes.
translations.idiomatic: whoever fears the city will fall may leave whenever he wishes."

sentences.zh: 」眾感其言，皆無異志。

translations.literal: " The crowd was moved by his words and none wavered.
translations.idiomatic: The men were moved by his words and none wavered.

sentences.zh: 魏主留閿鄉。

translations.literal: The Western Wei emperor remained at Wen township.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei emperor remained at Wen township.

sentences.zh: 丞相泰以士馬疲弊，不可速進，且謂青雀等烏合，不能為患，曰：「我至長安，以輕騎臨之，必當面縛。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yuwen Tai, because men and horses were worn out and could not advance quickly, and because he thought Qingque and the rest were a rabble that could do no harm, said, "When I reach Chang'an I will ride against them with light cavalry—they will surely be bound before me.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai, finding men and horses exhausted and unable to march fast, thought Qingque and the rest a rabble that could do no harm. He said, "When I reach Chang'an I will ride against them with light cavalry—they will be bound before me."

sentences.zh: 」通直散騎常侍吳郡陸通諫曰：「賊逆謀久定，必無遷善之心。

translations.literal: " Direct Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Tong of Wu commandery remonstrated, "The rebels' plot has long been fixed—they surely have no mind to mend their ways.
translations.idiomatic: Direct Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Lu Tong of Wu remonstrated, "The rebels' plot is long fixed—they have no mind to mend their ways.

sentences.zh: 蜂蠆有毒，安可輕也！

translations.literal: Wasps and scorpions have poison—how can they be treated lightly!
translations.idiomatic: Wasps and scorpions have poison—how can they be treated lightly!

sentences.zh: 且賊詐言東寇將至，今若以輕騎臨之，百姓謂為信然，益當驚擾。

translations.literal: Moreover the rebels falsely say an eastern enemy is coming; if you now ride against them with light cavalry, the people will take it for truth and grow more alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they falsely claim an eastern enemy is coming; if you ride against them with light cavalry, the people will believe it and grow more alarmed.

sentences.zh: 今軍雖疲弊，精銳尚多。

translations.literal: The army is weary, but elite troops remain in plenty.
translations.idiomatic: The army is weary, but plenty of elite troops remain.

sentences.zh: 以明公之威，總大軍以臨之，何憂不克！

translations.literal: With your lordship's prestige, lead the whole army against them—why fear you cannot overcome them!
translations.idiomatic: With your prestige, lead the whole army against them—why fear you cannot break them!

sentences.zh: 」泰從之，引兵西入。

translations.literal: " Yuwen Tai followed his advice and led his army west.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai took his advice and led his army west.

sentences.zh: 父老見泰至，莫不悲喜，士女相賀。

translations.literal: When the elders saw Yuwen Tai arrive, none failed to weep for joy; men and women congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: When the elders saw Yuwen Tai arrive, none failed to weep for joy; men and women congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 華州刺史宇文導引兵襲咸陽，斬思慶，擒伏德。

translations.literal: Hua province inspector Yuwen Dao led troops to strike Xianyang, beheaded Siqing, and captured Fude.
translations.idiomatic: Hua inspector Yuwen Dao struck Xianyang, beheaded Siqing, and captured Fude.

sentences.zh: 南度渭，與泰會攻青雀，破之。

translations.literal: He crossed the Wei southward, joined Yuwen Tai, and together attacked Qingque and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Wei southward, joined Yuwen Tai, and together broke Qingque.

sentences.zh: 太保梁景睿以疾留長安，與青雀通謀，泰殺之。

translations.literal: Grand Guardian Liang Jingrui, ill and left at Chang'an, conspired with Qingque; Yuwen Tai executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Guardian Liang Jingrui, ill and left at Chang'an, had conspired with Qingque; Yuwen Tai executed him.

sentences.zh: 東魏太師歡自晉陽將七千騎至孟津，未濟，聞魏師已循，遂濟河，遣別將追魏師至崤，不及而還。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Grand Mentor Gao Huan himself led seven thousand horsemen from Jinyang to Meng Ford; before he crossed, he heard the Western Wei army had already withdrawn, crossed the river, sent a detached force in pursuit to the Xiao Mountains, could not overtake them, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan himself led seven thousand horsemen from Jinyang to Meng Ford. Before he crossed, he heard the Western Wei army had already withdrawn; he crossed, sent a detachment in pursuit to the Xiao Mountains, could not overtake them, and returned.

sentences.zh: 歡攻金墉，長孫子彥棄城走，焚城中室屋俱盡，歡毀金墉而還。

translations.literal: Gao Huan attacked Jinyong; Changsun Ziyan abandoned the city and fled, burning every building within; Huan destroyed Jinyong and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan attacked Jinyong; Changsun Ziyan abandoned the city and fled, burning every building within; Huan razed Jinyong and returned.

sentences.zh: 東魏之遷鄴也，主客郎中裴讓之留洛陽。

translations.literal: When Eastern Wei moved the capital to Ye, Master of Guests Pei Rangzhi remained at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Wei moved the capital to Ye, Master of Guests Pei Rangzhi remained at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信之敗也，讓之弟諏之隨丞相泰入關，為大行台倉曹郎中。

translations.literal: When Dugu Xin was defeated, Rangzhi's younger brother Xunzhi followed Chancellor Yuwen Tai into Guanzhong and served as Grand Commissioner's clerk for granaries.
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Xin was defeated, Rangzhi's younger brother Xunzhi followed Yuwen Tai into Guanzhong and served as the Grand Commissioner's granary clerk.

sentences.zh: 歡囚讓之兄弟五人，讓之曰：「昔諸葛亮兄弟，事吳、蜀各盡其心，況讓之老母在此，不忠不孝，必不為也。

translations.literal: Gao Huan imprisoned all five Rangzhi brothers; Rangzhi said, "In old times Zhuge Liang's brothers served Wu and Shu each with all their hearts; moreover Rangzhi's old mother is here—disloyal and unfilial, they surely will not do it.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan imprisoned all five Rangzhi brothers. Rangzhi said, "In old times the Zhuge brothers served Wu and Shu each with all their hearts; and my old mother is here—disloyal and unfilial, we surely will not do it.

sentences.zh: 明公推誠待物，物亦歸心；

translations.literal: My lord treats men with sincere trust, and men return their hearts;
translations.idiomatic: My lord treats men with sincere trust, and men return their hearts;

sentences.zh: 若用猜忌，去霸業遠矣。

translations.literal: if you use suspicion instead, you are far from hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: use suspicion instead, and you are far from hegemony."

sentences.zh: 」歡皆釋之。

translations.literal: " Gao Huan released them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan released them all.

sentences.zh: 九月，魏主入長安，丞相泰還屯華州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Western Wei emperor entered Chang'an; Chancellor Yuwen Tai returned to camp at Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the Western Wei emperor entered Chang'an; Yuwen Tai returned to camp at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 東魏大都督賀拔仁擊邢磨納、盧仲禮等，平之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Grand Commander Heluoba Ren attacked Xing Monai, Lu Zhongli, and the rest and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei Grand Commander Heluoba Ren attacked Xing Monai, Lu Zhongli, and the rest and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 盧景裕本儒生，太師歡釋之，召館於家，使教諸子。

translations.literal: Lu Jingyu was originally a Confucian scholar; Grand Mentor Gao Huan released him and had him lodge at home to teach his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingyu was originally a Confucian scholar; Gao Huan released him, took him into his household, and had him teach his sons.

sentences.zh: 景裕講論精微，難者或相詆訶，大聲厲色，言至不遜，而景裕神采儼然，風調如一，從容往復，無際可尋。

translations.literal: Jingyu's discourse was subtle; when challengers sometimes reviled him with loud voice and harsh color, speech even to insolence, Jingyu's bearing remained grave, his tone unchanged, and he answered at ease back and forth with no seam to find.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu's discourse was subtle; when challengers sometimes reviled him with raised voice and harsh color, even to insolence, Jingyu's bearing stayed grave, his tone unchanged, and he answered at ease with no seam to find.

sentences.zh: 性清靜，歷官屢有進退，無得失之色；

translations.literal: By nature he was quiet; through repeated promotions and demotions in office he showed no sign of gain or loss;
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was quiet; through repeated promotions and demotions he showed no sign of gain or loss;

sentences.zh: 弊衣粗食，恬然自安，終日端嚴，如對賓客。

translations.literal: in worn clothes and coarse food he was content, all day upright as if facing guests.
translations.idiomatic: in worn clothes and coarse food he was content, all day upright as if facing guests.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，魏歸高敖曹、竇泰、莫多婁貸文之首於東魏。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Western Wei returned the heads of Gao Aocao, Dou Tai, and Mo Duo Lou Daiwen to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Western Wei returned the heads of Gao Aocao, Dou Tai, and Mo Duo Lou Daiwen to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍劉孝儀等聘於東魏。

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Xiaoyi and others went on a friendly mission to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Liu Xiaoyi and others went on a friendly mission to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏是雲寶襲洛陽，東魏洛州刺史王元軌棄城走。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Western Wei's Shi Yunbao raided Luoyang; Eastern Wei's Luo province inspector Wang Yuan Gui abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Western Wei's Shi Yunbao raided Luoyang; Eastern Wei's Luo inspector Wang Yuan Gui abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 都督趙剛襲廣州，拔之。

translations.literal: Commander Zhao Gang raided Guang province and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zhao Gang raided Guang province and took it.

sentences.zh: 於是自襄、廣已西城鎮復為魏。

translations.literal: From Xiang and Guang westward the frontier garrisons thus returned to Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: From Xiang and Guang westward the frontier garrisons thus returned to Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏自正光以後，四方多事，民避賦役，多為僧尼，至二百萬人，寺有三萬餘區。

translations.literal: Since the Zhenguang era Western Wei had been beset on every side; to escape taxes and corvée many became monks and nuns—up to two million persons, with more than thirty thousand monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Zhenguang era Western Wei had been beset on every side; to escape taxes and corvée many became monks and nuns—up to two million persons and more than thirty thousand monasteries.

sentences.zh: 至是，東魏始詔「牧守、令長擅立寺者，計其功庸，以枉法論。

translations.literal: Now Eastern Wei for the first time decreed, "Pasture chiefs and district magistrates who on their own authority establish monasteries shall have their merit reckoned and be punished as bending the law.
translations.idiomatic: Now Eastern Wei for the first time decreed that pasture chiefs and district magistrates who established monasteries on their own authority would have their merit reckoned and be punished for bending the law.

sentences.zh: 初，魏伊川土豪李長壽為防蠻都督，積功至北華州刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Changshou, a powerful man of the Yi River in Western Wei, had been Defense Commander against the Man and through accumulated merit rose to Northern Hua province inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Changshou, a powerful man of the Yi River in Western Wei, had been Defense Commander against the Man and through merit rose to Northern Hua inspector.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝西遷，長壽帥其徒拒東魏，魏以長壽為廣州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Changshou led his followers to resist Eastern Wei; Western Wei made Changshou Guang province inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Changshou led his followers against Eastern Wei; Western Wei made him Guang inspector.

sentences.zh: 侯景攻拔其壁，殺之。

translations.literal: Hou Jing stormed his fort, killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing stormed his fort and killed him.

sentences.zh: 其子延孫復收集父兵以拒東魏，魏之貴臣廣陵王欣、錄尚書長孫稚等皆攜家往依之，延孫資遣衛送，使達關中。

translations.literal: His son Yansun gathered his father's troops again to resist Eastern Wei; Western Wei's great ministers, the Prince of Guangling Xin and Recorder of the Masters of Writing Changsun Zhi and others, all brought their families to rely on him; Yansun supplied and escorted them until they reached Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yansun gathered his father's troops again to resist Eastern Wei; Western Wei's great ministers—the Prince of Guangling Xin, Recorder Changsun Zhi, and others—all brought their families to him; Yansun supplied and escorted them to Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 東魏高歡患之，數遣兵攻延孫，不能克。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei's Gao Huan was troubled by this and repeatedly sent troops against Yansun but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was troubled by this and repeatedly sent troops against Yansun but could not overcome him.

sentences.zh: 魏以延孫為京南行台、節度河南諸軍事、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Western Wei made Yansun Southern Capital Route Grand Commissioner, commander of all military affairs south of the river in Henan, and Guang province inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei made Yansun Southern Capital Route Grand Commissioner, commander of Henan military affairs south of the river, and Guang inspector.

sentences.zh: 延孫以澄清伊、洛為己任，魏以延孫兵少，更以長壽之婿京兆韋法保為東洛州刺史，配兵數百以助之。

translations.literal: Yansun took clearing the Yi and Luo as his charge; Western Wei, because Yansun had few troops, further made Changshou's son-in-law Wei Fabao of Jingzhao Eastern Luo inspector and assigned him several hundred soldiers to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Yansun took clearing the Yi and Luo as his charge; Western Wei, finding him short of troops, further made Changshou's son-in-law Wei Fabao of Jingzhao Eastern Luo inspector and gave him several hundred men to assist.

sentences.zh: 法保名祐，以字行，既至，與延孫連兵置柵於伏流。

translations.literal: Fabao's given name was You; he went by his style; when he arrived he joined Yansun in linking camps at Fuliou.
translations.idiomatic: Fabao's given name was You; he went by his style. When he arrived he joined Yansun in linking camps at Fuliou.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信之入洛陽也，欲繕修宮室，使外兵郎中天水權景宣帥徒兵三千出采運。

translations.literal: When Dugu Xin entered Luoyang he wished to repair the palaces and sent Outer Troops Gentleman Quan Jingxuan of Tianshui to lead three thousand laborers out to gather transport timber.
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Xin entered Luoyang he wished to repair the palaces and sent Outer Troops Gentleman Quan Jingxuan of Tianshui to lead three thousand laborers out for timber.

sentences.zh: 會東魏兵至，河南皆叛，景宣間道西走，與李延孫相會，攻孔城，拔之，洛陽以南尋亦西附。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei troops arrived; all south of the river rebelled; Jingxuan took a hidden path west, met Yansun, attacked Kong city, took it, and south of Luoyang soon submitted westward again.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei troops arrived; all south of the river rebelled. Jingxuan took a hidden path west, met Yansun, attacked Kong city and took it; south of Luoyang soon submitted westward again.

sentences.zh: 丞相泰即留景宣守張白塢，節度東南諸軍應關西者。

translations.literal: Chancellor Yuwen Tai at once left Jingxuan to hold Zhangbai Stockade and command southeastern military affairs responding to Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai left Jingxuan to hold Zhangbai Stockade and command southeastern forces answering Guanxi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，延孫為其長史楊伯蘭所殺，韋法保即引兵據延孫之柵。

translations.literal: That year Yansun was killed by his chief clerk Yang Bolan; Wei Fabao at once led troops to hold Yansun's stockade.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yansun was killed by his chief clerk Yang Bolan; Wei Fabao at once led troops to hold Yansun's stockade.

sentences.zh: 東魏將段琛等據宜陽，遣陽州刺史牛道恆誘魏邊民。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei generals Duan Chen and others held Yiyang and sent Yang province inspector Niu Daoheng to entice Western Wei border people.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei generals Duan Chen and others held Yiyang and sent Yang inspector Niu Daoheng to entice Western Wei border people.

sentences.zh: 魏南兗州刺史韋孝寬患之，乃詐為道恆與孝寬書，論歸款之意，使諜人遺之於琛營，琛果疑道恆。

translations.literal: Southern Yan province inspector Wei Xiaokuan was troubled by this; he forged a letter in Daoheng's name to Xiaokuan discussing surrender, and had a spy leave it in Chen's camp; Chen indeed suspected Daoheng.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Yan inspector Wei Xiaokuan was troubled by this. He forged a letter in Daoheng's name to Xiaokuan discussing surrender and had a spy leave it in Chen's camp; Chen indeed suspected Daoheng.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乘其猜阻，出兵襲之，擒道恆及琛，崤、澠遂清。

translations.literal: Xiaokuan exploited their mutual suspicion, sent troops to strike, captured Daoheng and Chen, and the Xiao and Mian routes were cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaokuan exploited their suspicion, struck, captured Daoheng and Chen, and the Xiao and Mian routes were cleared.

sentences.zh: 東道行台王思政以玉壁險要，請築城，自恆農徙鎮之，詔加都督汾、晉、并州諸軍事、并州刺史，行台如故。

translations.literal: Eastern Route Grand Commissioner Wang Sizheng, because Yubi was strategically vital, asked to build a fortress; he moved his garrison from Hengnong; he was further made commander of Fen, Jin, and Bing military affairs and Bing province inspector, his Grand Commission unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Route Grand Commissioner Wang Sizheng, finding Yubi strategically vital, asked to build a fortress and moved his garrison from Hengnong; he was further made commander of Fen, Jin, and Bing military affairs and Bing inspector, his Grand Commission unchanged.

sentences.zh: 東魏以高澄攝吏部尚書，始改崔亮年勞之制，銓擢賢能；

translations.literal: Eastern Wei put Gao Cheng in charge of the Ministry of Personnel and for the first time changed Cui Liang's seniority system, selecting and promoting the able;
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei put Gao Cheng in charge of the Ministry of Personnel, for the first time changed Cui Liang's seniority system, and selected and promoted the able;

sentences.zh: 又沙汰尚書郎，妙選人地以充之。

translations.literal: they also sifted Masters of Writing gentlemen, choosing men of fine talent and background to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: they also sifted Masters of Writing posts, choosing men of fine talent and background to fill them.

sentences.zh: 凡才名之士，雖未薦擢，皆引致門下，與之遊宴、講論、賦詩，士大夫以是稱之。

translations.literal: Men of talent and name, though not yet promoted, were all brought to his gate, entertained, debated with, and made to compose poetry; scholar-officials therefore praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Men of talent and name, though not yet promoted, were all brought to his gate for feasting, debate, and poetry; scholar-officials therefore praised him.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝十四大同五年（

translations.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Wu, year 15 of the Datong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, fifteenth year of Datong (

sentences.zh: 己未，公元五三九年）

translations.literal: jiwei, 539 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiwei, AD 539)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙卯，以尚書左僕射蕭淵藻為中衛將軍，丹楊尹何敬容為尚書令，吏部尚書張纘為僕射。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on yimao, Left Vice Director Xiao Yuanzao was made Central Guard General, Danyang governor He Jingrong was made Director of the Masters of Writing, and Ministry of Personnel Director Zhang Zuan was made Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on yimao, Left Vice Director Xiao Yuanzao was made Central Guard General, Danyang governor He Jingrong Director of the Masters of Writing, and Ministry of Personnel Director Zhang Zuan Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 纘，弘策之子也。

translations.literal: Zuan was the son of Hongce.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan was the son of Hongce.

sentences.zh: 自晉、宋以來，宰相皆以文義自逸，敬容獨勤簿領，日旰不休，為時俗所嗤鄙。

translations.literal: Since Jin and Song, chancellors had all taken their ease in literary refinement; Jingrong alone toiled at ledgers, working from dawn unceasing, and was scorned by the fashion of the day.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin and Song, chancellors had all taken their ease in literary refinement; Jingrong alone toiled at ledgers from dawn unceasing, and the fashion of the day scorned him.

sentences.zh: 自徐勉、周捨既卒，當權要者，外朝則何敬容，內省則朱異。

translations.literal: After Xu Mian and Zhou She died, those who held power were Jingrong in the outer court and Zhu Yi in the inner.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Mian and Zhou She died, power lay with Jingrong in the outer court and Zhu Yi in the inner.

sentences.zh: 敬容質愨無文，以綱維為己任；

translations.literal: Jingrong was plain and without literary polish, taking the framework of rule as his charge;
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong was plain and without literary polish, taking the framework of rule as his charge;

sentences.zh: 異文華敏洽，曲營世譽。

translations.literal: Yi was refined, quick, and skilled at currying worldly favor.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was refined, quick, and skilled at currying worldly favor.

sentences.zh: 二人行異而俱得幸於上。

translations.literal: The two differed in conduct yet both won the sovereign's favor.
translations.idiomatic: The two differed in conduct yet both won the sovereign's favor.

sentences.zh: 異善伺候人主意為阿諛，用事三十年，廣納貨賂，欺罔視聽，遠近莫不忿疾。

translations.literal: Yi was skilled at watching the sovereign's mind and flattering it; for thirty years he held power, took bribes widely, deceived what the sovereign saw and heard, and near and far alike burned with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was skilled at watching the sovereign's mind and flattering it; for thirty years he held power, took bribes widely, deceived what the sovereign saw and heard, and near and far burned with resentment.

sentences.zh: 園宅、玩好、飲膳、聲色窮一時之盛。

translations.literal: His gardens, treasures, food, drink, and music exhausted the splendor of the age.
translations.idiomatic: His gardens, treasures, food, drink, and music exhausted the splendor of the age.

sentences.zh: 每休下，車馬填門，唯王承、王稚及褚翔不往。

translations.literal: Whenever he left office his gate was jammed with carriages and horses; only Wang Cheng, Wang Zhi, and Chu Xiang did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he left office his gate was jammed with carriages; only Wang Cheng, Wang Zhi, and Chu Xiang did not go.

sentences.zh: 承、稚，暕之子；

translations.literal: Cheng and Zhi were sons of Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Zhi were sons of Yan;

sentences.zh: 翔，淵之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Xiang was a great-grandson of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was a great-grandson of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，御史中丞參禮儀事賀琛奏：「南、北二郊及藉田，往還並宜御輦，不復乘輅。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Censor-in-Chief He Chen, participating in ritual affairs, memorialized, "The southern and northern suburban sacrifices and the plowing of the sacred field should all use the imperial carriage and no longer ride the ceremonial chariot.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Censor-in-Chief He Chen, participating in ritual affairs, memorialized that the southern and northern suburban sacrifices and the plowing of the sacred field should all use the imperial carriage and no longer the ceremonial chariot.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之，祀宗廟仍乘玉輦。

translations.literal: " The edict followed this; for ancestral temple sacrifice the jade carriage was still used.
translations.idiomatic: The edict followed this; for ancestral temple sacrifice the jade carriage was still used.

sentences.zh: 琛，瑒之弟子也。

translations.literal: Chen was a nephew's son of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was a nephew's son of Yang.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，東魏以尚書令孫騰為司徒。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Eastern Wei made Director of the Masters of Writing Sun Teng Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Eastern Wei made Director of the Masters of Writing Sun Teng Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 辛未，上祀南郊。

translations.literal: On xinwei, the sovereign sacrificed at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the Liang sovereign sacrificed at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 魏丞相泰於行台置學，取丞郎、府佐德行明敏者充學生，悉令旦治公務，晚就講習。

translations.literal: Western Wei Chancellor Yuwen Tai established a school at the Grand Commission, taking Masters of Writing gentlemen and Grand Commission aides of clear conduct and keen mind as students, all to handle public business by day and attend lectures by evening.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai established a school at the Grand Commission, taking Masters of Writing gentlemen and Grand Commission aides of clear conduct and keen mind as students to handle public business by day and attend lectures by evening.

sentences.zh: 東魏丞相歡，以徐州刺史房謨、廣平太守羊孰、廣宗太守竇瑗、平原太守許惇有政績清能，與諸刺史書，褒稱謨等以勸之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Chancellor Gao Huan, because Xu province inspector Fang Mo, Guangping governor Yang Shu, Guangzong governor Dou Yuan, and Pingyuan governor Xu Dun had achievements in governance and were pure and able, wrote all the inspectors a letter praising Mo and the rest to encourage them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, because Xu inspector Fang Mo, Guangping governor Yang Shu, Guangzong governor Dou Yuan, and Pingyuan governor Xu Dun had clean records and ability, wrote all the inspectors praising Mo and the rest to encourage them.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，甲戌，東魏立丞相歡女為皇后；

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on jiaxu, Eastern Wei installed Chancellor Gao Huan's daughter as empress;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, on jiaxu Eastern Wei installed Gao Huan's daughter as empress;

sentences.zh: 乙亥，大赦。

translations.literal: on yihai, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: on yihai a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 魏以開府儀同三司李弼為司空。

translations.literal: Western Wei made Kaifu Yitong Sansi Li Bi Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei made Li Bi Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏以扶風王孚為太尉。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Western Wei made the Prince of Fufeng, Fu, Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Western Wei made the Prince of Fufeng, Fu, Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲子，東魏發畿內十萬人城鄴，四十日罷。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiazi, Eastern Wei mobilized one hundred thousand men within the capital circuit to wall Ye; the work ended in forty days.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiazi Eastern Wei mobilized one hundred thousand men within the capital circuit to wall Ye; the work ended in forty days.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸亥，以新宮成，大赦，改元興和。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guihai, because the new palace was completed, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Xinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on guihai, because the new palace was completed, a general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name changed to Xinghe.

sentences.zh: 魏置紙筆於陽武門外以求得失。

translations.literal: Western Wei placed brush and paper outside Yangwu Gate to seek the people's gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei placed brush and paper outside Yangwu Gate to seek the people's gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙亥，東魏使散騎常侍王元景、魏收來聘。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on yihai, Eastern Wei sent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Yuanjing and Wei Shou on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yihai Eastern Wei sent Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Yuanjing and Wei Shou on a friendly mission.

sentences.zh: 東魏人以《正光歷》浸差，命校書郎李業興更加修正，以甲子為元，號曰《興光歷》，既成，行之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei, because the Zhenguang calendar had gradually drifted, ordered collator Li Yexing to revise it further, taking jiazi as origin and naming it the Xingguang calendar; when it was done, it was put in use.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei, finding the Zhenguang calendar had drifted, ordered collator Li Yexing to revise it, taking jiazi as origin and naming it the Xingguang calendar; when done, it was put in use.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍朱異奏：「頃來置州稍廣，而小大不倫，請分為五品，其位秩高卑，參僚多少，皆以是為差。

translations.literal: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhu Yi memorialized, "Recently the establishment of provinces has grown somewhat broad, large and small not in proper order; I ask that they be divided into five grades, with rank, salary, and number of staff all differentiated thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhu Yi memorialized, "Recently provinces have multiplied without proper order; I ask that they be divided into five grades, with rank, salary, and staff all set thereby."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " The edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict followed this.

sentences.zh: 於是上品二十州，次品十州，次品八州，次品二十三州，下品二十一州。

translations.literal: Thus there were twenty provinces of the highest grade, ten of the second, eight of the third, twenty-three of the fourth, and twenty-one of the lowest.
translations.idiomatic: Thus there were twenty provinces of the highest grade, ten of the second, eight of the third, twenty-three of the fourth, and twenty-one of the lowest.

sentences.zh: 時上方事征伐，恢拓境宇，北逾淮、汝，東距彭城，西開牂柯，南平俚洞，建置州郡，紛綸甚眾，故異請分之。

translations.literal: At the time the sovereign was engaged in campaigns, expanding territory; north beyond the Huai and Ru, east to Pengcheng, west opening Zangke, south pacifying the Li caves—provinces and commanderies were established in profusion, and therefore Yi asked to divide them.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign was then campaigning, expanding territory—north beyond the Huai and Ru, east to Pengcheng, west into Zangke, south pacifying the Li caves—provinces and commanderies multiplied in profusion, and therefore Yi asked to grade them.

sentences.zh: 其下品皆異國之人來歸附者，徒有州名而無土地，或因荒徼之民所居村落置州及郡縣，刺史守令皆用彼人為之，尚書不能悉領，山川險遠，職貢罕通。

translations.literal: Those of the lowest grade were all men of foreign states who came to submit; they had only the name of a province and no land, or provinces and districts were set up on villages where frontier people dwelt; inspectors and magistrates were all drawn from those people; the Masters of Writing could not fully oversee them; mountains and rivers were perilous and far, tribute rarely reached.
translations.idiomatic: The lowest grade were foreigners who had submitted—provinces in name only, without land—or provinces and districts set on frontier villages; inspectors and magistrates were drawn from those peoples; the Masters of Writing could not fully oversee them; mountains were perilous and tribute rarely came.

sentences.zh: 五品之外，又有二十餘州不知處所。

translations.literal: Beyond the five grades there were more than twenty provinces whose location was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the five grades more than twenty provinces had no known location.

sentences.zh: 凡一百七州。

translations.literal: In all there were one hundred seven provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In all there were one hundred seven provinces.

sentences.zh: 又以邊境鎮戍，雖領民不多，欲重其將帥，皆建為郡，或一人領二三郡太守，州郡雖多而戶口日耗矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, because frontier garrisons, though they ruled few people, wished to weight their commanders, all were made into commanderies, or one man held two or three commanderies as governor; though provinces and commanderies multiplied, households daily dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover frontier garrisons, though they ruled few people, were weighted by making them commanderies, or one man held two or three commanderies; provinces and commanderies multiplied while households daily dwindled.

sentences.zh: 魏自西遷以來，禮樂散逸，丞相泰命左僕射周惠達、吏部郎中北海唐瑾損益舊章，至是稍備。

translations.literal: Since Western Wei's move west, ritual and music had scattered; Chancellor Yuwen Tai ordered Left Vice Director Zhou Huida and Ministry of Personnel gentleman Tang Jin of Beihai to trim and augment the old regulations; by now they were somewhat complete.
translations.idiomatic: Since Western Wei's move west, ritual and music had scattered; Yuwen Tai ordered Zhou Huida and Ministry of Personnel gentleman Tang Jin of Beihai to trim the old regulations; by now they were somewhat complete.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝十四大同六年（

translations.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Wu, year 16 of the Datong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, sixteenth year of Datong (

sentences.zh: 庚申，公元五四零年）

translations.literal: gengshen, 540 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengshen, AD 540)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬申，東魏以廣平公庫狄干為太保。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renshen, Eastern Wei made Duke of Guangping Kudi Gan Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renshen Eastern Wei made Kudi Gan, Duke of Guangping, Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，東魏主入新宮，大赦。

translations.literal: On dingchou, the Eastern Wei ruler entered the new palace and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou the Eastern Wei ruler entered the new palace and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 魏扶風王孚卒。

translations.literal: Western Wei's Prince of Fufeng, Fu, died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fu of Fufeng in Western Wei died.

sentences.zh: 二月，己亥，上耕藉田。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jihai, the emperor plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jihai, the Liang emperor plowed the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 魏鑄五銖錢。

translations.literal: Western Wei cast wuzhu coins.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei cast wuzhu coins.

sentences.zh: 東魏大行台侯景出三鴉，將復荊州，魏丞相泰遣李弼、獨孤信各將五千騎出武關，景乃還。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Grand Mobile Headquarters Hou Jing marched from Sanya intending to recover Jing province; Western Wei Chancellor Tai sent Li Bi and Dugu Xin, each with five thousand horse, out through Wuguan, and Jing withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing of Eastern Wei marched from Sanya to recover Jing; Yuwen Tai sent Li Bi and Dugu Xin, each with five thousand horse, through Wuguan, and Jing turned back.

sentences.zh: 魏文後既為尼，居別宮，悼後猶忌之，乃以其子武都王戊為秦州刺史，使文後隨之官。

translations.literal: The Wen Empress of Wei had become a nun and lived in a separate palace; the Dowager Empress still resented her and made her son, Prince Wu of Wudu, inspector of Qin, ordering the Wen Empress to go with him to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wen had taken the veil and lived apart; Dowager Empress Diao still hated her and sent her son Prince Wu of Wudu to Qin as inspector, making Wen Empress go with him.

sentences.zh: 魏主雖限以大計，而恩好不忘，密令養發，有追還之意。

translations.literal: Though the Wei sovereign was bound by the great plan, he did not forget old affection and secretly ordered her hair to be allowed to grow again, with intent to recall her.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Wei emperor was held to the great plan but did not forget her; secretly he let her hair grow again, meaning to bring her back.

sentences.zh: 會柔然舉國度河南侵，時頗有言柔然以悼後故興師者，帝曰：「豈有興百萬之眾為一女子邪！

translations.literal: It happened that Rouran crossed the Yellow River in full strength to raid; at the time many said Rouran had raised arms for the dowager empress's sake. The emperor said, "Would anyone raise a million men for one woman!
translations.idiomatic: Rouran crossed the river in full strength to raid; many said they came for the dowager empress. The emperor said, "Who raises a million men for one woman!

sentences.zh: 雖然，致人此言，朕亦何顏以見將帥！

translations.literal: Still, that men should say this—what face have I to show the generals!
translations.idiomatic: Yet that such talk should spread—what face have I before my generals!

sentences.zh: 」乃遣中常侍曹寵繼手敕賜文後自盡。

translations.literal: " He then sent Palace Attendant Cao Chong with an edict in his own hand ordering the Wen Empress to take her own life.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Palace Attendant Cao Chong with a handwritten edict ordering Wen Empress to die by her own hand.

sentences.zh: 文後泣謂寵曰：「願至尊千萬歲，天下康寧，死無恨也！

translations.literal: The Wen Empress wept and told Chong, "May His Majesty live ten thousand years and the realm be at peace—I die without regret!
translations.idiomatic: Wen Empress wept and told Chong, "May His Majesty live ten thousand years and all under Heaven be at peace—I die without regret!

sentences.zh: 」遂自殺。

translations.literal: " She then killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: " She then killed herself.

sentences.zh: 鑿麥積崖而葬之，號曰寂陵。

translations.literal: They carved out Maiji Cliff to bury her and called the tomb Silent Mound.
translations.idiomatic: They hollowed Maiji Cliff for her tomb and called it Silent Mound.

sentences.zh: 夏，丞相泰召諸軍屯沙苑以備柔然。

translations.literal: In summer, Chancellor Tai summoned the armies to camp at Shayuan against Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, Yuwen Tai gathered the armies at Shayuan against Rouran.

sentences.zh: 右僕射周惠達發士馬守京城，塹諸街巷，召雍州刺史王羆議之，羆不應召，謂使者曰：「若蠕蠕至渭北者，王羆自帥鄉里破之，不煩國家兵馬，何為天子城中作如此驚擾！

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Zhou Huida mobilized troops and horses to guard the capital, trenched the streets and lanes, and summoned Yongzhou inspector Wang Pi to counsel; Pi did not answer the summons and told the envoy, "If the Rouran reach north of the Wei, Wang Pi himself will lead the countryside to break them—why trouble the state's troops and alarm the Son of Heaven's city like this!
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huida, Right Vice Director, mobilized troops for the capital, trenched the streets, and summoned Wang Pi of Yongzhou; Pi would not come and told the envoy, "If Rouran reach north of the Wei, Wang Pi will break them with his own district—why alarm the capital with state troops!

sentences.zh: 由周家小兒恇怯致此。

translations.literal: This comes of the Zhou family's cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: This is the Zhou household's cowardice.

sentences.zh: 」柔然至夏州而退。

translations.literal: " Rouran reached Xia province and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Rouran reached Xia province and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 未幾，悼後遇疾殂。

translations.literal: Before long the Dowager Empress fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Dowager Empress Diao fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 五月，乙酉，魏行台宮延和、陝州刺史宮延慶降於東魏，東魏以河北馬場為義州以處之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on yiyou, Western Wei Mobile Headquarters Gong Yanhe and Shaan inspector Gong Yanqing surrendered to Eastern Wei; Eastern Wei made the Hebei horse pastures into Yi province to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on yiyou, Gong Yanhe of Western Wei's mobile headquarters and Gong Yanqing, inspector of Shaan, surrendered to Eastern Wei, which made the Hebei horse pastures into Yi province to house them.

sentences.zh: 東魏陽州武公高永樂卒。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei's Duke of Yang province, Gao Yongle, died.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yongle, Duke of Yang province in Eastern Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 閏月，丁丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on dingchou the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on dingchou the new moon, there was an eclipse of the sun.

sentences.zh: 己丑，東魏封皇兄景植為宜陽王，皇弟威為清河王，謙為穎川王。

translations.literal: On jichou, Eastern Wei enfeoffed the emperor's elder brother Jingzhi as Prince of Yiyang and younger brothers Wei as Prince of Qinghe and Qian as Prince of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Eastern Wei made the emperor's elder brother Jingzhi Prince of Yiyang and younger brothers Wei Prince of Qinghe and Qian Prince of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬子，東魏華山王鷙卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on renzi, Eastern Wei's Prince of Huashan, Zhi, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on renzi, Prince Zhi of Huashan in Eastern Wei died.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁亥，東魏使兼散騎常侍李象等來聘。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on dinghai, Eastern Wei sent Associate Bearer of the Staff Li Xiang and others on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dinghai, Eastern Wei sent Li Xiang and others as envoys.

sentences.zh: 八月，戊午，大赦。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on wuwu, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wuwu, the Liang emperor proclaimed amnesty.

sentences.zh: 九月，戊戌，司空袁昂卒，遺疏不受贈謚，敕諸子勿上行狀及立銘志。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on wuxu, Minister of Works Yuan Ang died; in his final memorial he refused posthumous gifts and titles and charged his sons not to submit a funeral report or set up an inscription.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on wuxu, Minister of Works Yuan Ang died; his last memorial refused posthumous honors and forbade his sons to file a funeral report or raise a stele.

sentences.zh: 上不許，贈本官，謚穆正公。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it and posthumously gave his former office with the posthumous title Pure and Upright Duke.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor would not allow it and gave his former rank with the posthumous title Duke Pure and Upright.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，魏太師念賢卒。

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, Western Wei Grand Tutor Nian Xian died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, Nian Xian, Grand Tutor of Western Wei, died.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾自莫折念生之亂，不通於魏。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun, since Mohe Niansheng's rebellion, had had no dealings with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun, since Mohe Niansheng's rebellion, had broken contact with Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 伏連籌卒，子誇呂立，始稱可汗，居伏俟城。

translations.literal: Fulianchou died and his son Kualü succeeded, first taking the title khan and dwelling at Fuhou city.
translations.idiomatic: Fulianchou died; his son Kualü succeeded, first styled himself khan, and dwelt at Fuhou city.

sentences.zh: 其地東西三千里，南北千餘里，官有王、公、僕射、尚書、郎中、將軍之號。

translations.literal: His lands stretched three thousand li east and west and more than a thousand north and south; offices bore the titles king, duke, steward, secretary, gentleman, and general.
translations.idiomatic: His realm ran three thousand li east to west and more than a thousand north to south, with offices titled king, duke, steward, secretary, gentleman, and general.

sentences.zh: 是歲，始遣使假道柔然，聘於東魏。

translations.literal: That year he first sent envoys by way of Rouran on a friendly mission to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year he first sent envoys through Rouran to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝十四大同七年（

translations.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Wu, year 7 of the Datong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, seventh year of Datong (

sentences.zh: 辛酉，公元五四一年）

translations.literal: xinyou, 541 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinyou, AD 541)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛巳，上祀南郊，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinsi, the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinsi, the Liang emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and proclaimed amnesty.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，祀明堂。

translations.literal: On xinchou he sacrificed at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou he sacrificed at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 宕昌王梁企定為其下所殺，弟彌定立。

translations.literal: Tanchang king Liang Qiding was killed by his subordinates; his younger brother Midian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: King Qiding of Tanchang was killed by his men; his brother Midian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙巳，以彌定為河、梁二州刺史、宕昌王。

translations.literal: In the second month, on yisi, Midian was made inspector of He and Liang provinces and king of Tanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yisi, Midian was made inspector of He and Liang and king of Tanchang.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，上耕藉田。

translations.literal: On xinhai the emperor plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the Liang emperor plowed the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 魏幽州刺史順陽王仲景坐事賜死。

translations.literal: Western Wei's Youzhou inspector, Prince of Shunyang, Zhongjing, was ordered to death for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing, Prince of Shunyang and inspector of Youzhou in Western Wei, was ordered to die for an offense.

sentences.zh: 三月，魏夏州刺史劉平伏據上郡反，大都督於謹討擒之。

translations.literal: In the third month, Western Wei's Xiazhou inspector Liu Pingfu held Shang commandery in rebellion; Grand Commander Yu Jin captured him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Liu Pingfu, inspector of Xia in Western Wei, rebelled at Shang commandery; Yu Jin captured him.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，遣兼散騎常侍明少遐等聘於東魏。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, Associate Bearer of the Staff Ming Shaoxia and others were sent on a friendly mission to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, Ming Shaoxia and others were sent as envoys to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，己卯，東魏宜陽王景植卒。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jimao, Eastern Wei's Prince of Yiyang, Jingzhi, died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jimao, Prince Jingzhi of Yiyang in Eastern Wei died.

sentences.zh: 魏以侍中宇文測為大都督、行汾州事。

translations.literal: Western Wei made Palace Attendant Yuwen Ce Grand Commander and acting inspector of Fen.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei made Palace Attendant Yuwen Ce Grand Commander with acting charge of Fen.

sentences.zh: 測，深之兄也，為政簡惠，得士民心。

translations.literal: Ce was Shen's elder brother; his government was simple and kind and won officers and people alike.
translations.idiomatic: Ce was Shen's elder brother; his rule was spare and kind and won officers and people alike.

sentences.zh: 地接東魏，東魏人數來寇抄，測擒獲之，命解縛，引與相見，為設酒殽，待以客禮，並給糧餼，衛送出境。

translations.literal: His territory bordered Eastern Wei; Eastern Wei men often came to raid; Ce captured them, ordered their bonds undone, received them face to face, set out wine and meat, treated them as guests, and gave grain and fodder, escorting them beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: His border touched Eastern Wei; raiders came often. Ce took them, had bonds cut, feasted them as guests, gave grain and fodder, and escorted them out.

sentences.zh: 東魏人大慚，不復為寇，汾、晉之間遂通慶吊，時論稱之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei men were deeply ashamed and raided no more; between Fen and Jin congratulations and condolences flowed freely, and men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The easterners were ashamed and raided no more; Fen and Jin exchanged congratulations and condolences, and the age praised him.

sentences.zh: 或告測交通境外者，丞相泰怒曰：「測為我安邊，我知其志，何得間我骨肉！

translations.literal: Someone reported that Ce had dealings beyond the border; Chancellor Tai grew angry and said, "Ce secures my frontier for me—I know his heart. How dare you come between my own flesh!
translations.idiomatic: Someone accused Ce of traffic beyond the border. Yuwen Tai raged: "Ce holds my frontier—I know his heart. Who dares set kin against kin!

sentences.zh: 」命斬之。

translations.literal: " He ordered the accuser beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: " He had the accuser beheaded.

sentences.zh: 魏丞相泰欲革易時政，為強國富民之法，大行台度支尚書兼司農卿蘇綽盡其智能，贊成其事，減官員，置二長，並置屯田以資軍國。

translations.literal: Western Wei Chancellor Tai wished to reform the government of the time and enact laws to strengthen the state and enrich the people; Grand Mobile Headquarters Director of Revenue and concurrent Minister of Agriculture Su Chuo gave all his wit to assist and complete the work—reducing officials, establishing two chiefs, and setting up garrison fields to supply army and state.
