translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai wished to reform government and enrich the state; Su Chuo of the grand mobile headquarters gave all his wit—fewer officials, two chiefs, garrison fields for army and state.

sentences.zh: 又為六條詔書，九月，始奏行之：一曰清心，二曰敦教化，三曰盡地利，四曰擢賢良，五曰恤獄訟，六曰均賦役。

translations.literal: He also drafted six articles of edict; in the ninth month they were first submitted and put into practice: first, purify the heart; second, thickly teach transformation; third, exhaust the land's advantage; fourth, promote the worthy; fifth, pity lawsuits; sixth, equalize levies and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted six articles of edict; in the ninth month they took force: purify the heart; teach transformation; use the land; promote worthies; pity lawsuits; equalize levies and corvée.

sentences.zh: 泰甚重之，嘗置諸坐右，又令百司習誦之，其牧守令長非通六條及計帳者，不得居官。

translations.literal: Tai greatly valued them, often kept them at his right hand, and ordered the hundred offices to study and recite them; prefects, defenders, magistrates, and chiefs who did not master the six articles and the accounts could not hold office.
translations.idiomatic: Tai prized them, kept them at hand, and made every office recite them; no magistrate who failed the six articles and the accounts could keep his post.

sentences.zh: 東魏詔群官於麟趾閣議定法制，謂之《麟趾格》，冬，十月，甲寅，頒行之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei ordered the officials to fix law at the Unicorn Toe Pavilion—called the Unicorn Toe Code; in winter, the tenth month, on jiayin, it was promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei had officials fix law at the Unicorn Toe Pavilion—the Unicorn Toe Code; in winter, the tenth month, on jiayin, it was promulgated.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，東魏發夫五萬築漳濱堰，三十五日罷。

translations.literal: On yisi Eastern Wei drafted fifty thousand laborers to build the Zhang embankment; in thirty-five days the work stopped.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Eastern Wei drafted fifty thousand men for the Zhang embankment; in thirty-five days the work stopped.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙戌，東魏以彭城王韶為太尉，度支尚書胡僧敬為司空。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingxu, Eastern Wei made Prince Shao of Pengcheng Grand Commandant and Director of Revenue Hu Sengjing Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingxu, Eastern Wei made Prince Shao of Pengcheng Grand Commandant and Hu Sengjing, Director of Revenue, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 僧敬名虔，以字行，國珍之兄孫，東魏主之舅也。

translations.literal: Sengjing's given name was Qian; he went by his style; he was National Treasure's elder brother's grandson and the Eastern Wei sovereign's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Sengjing styled Qian and was National Treasure's grand-nephew and the Eastern Wei emperor's uncle on the mother's side.

sentences.zh: 十二月，東魏遣兼散騎常侍李騫來聘。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Eastern Wei sent Associate Bearer of the Staff Li Qian on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Eastern Wei sent Li Qian as envoy.

sentences.zh: 交趾李賁世為豪右，仕不得志。

translations.literal: Li Ben of Jiaozhi had been a great house for generations; he could not advance in office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ben of Jiaozhi was a great house for generations but could not rise in office.

sentences.zh: 有並韶者，富於詞藻，詣選求官，吏部尚書蔡撙以並姓無前賢，除廣陽門郎；

translations.literal: There was one Bing Shao, rich in letters; he sought office through selection; Minister of Personnel Cai Bo, because the Bing surname had no former worthies, made him Gentleman at the Guangyang Gate;
translations.idiomatic: Bing Shao, rich in letters, sought office; Cai Bo of Personnel, because the Bing had no former worthies, made him Gentleman at the Guangyang Gate;

sentences.zh: 韶恥之。

translations.literal: Shao was shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was shamed.

sentences.zh: 賁與韶還鄉里，謀作亂，會交州刺史武林侯咨以刻暴失眾心，時賁監德州，因連結數州豪傑俱反。

translations.literal: Ben and Shao returned to their native place and plotted rebellion; it happened that Jiaozhi inspector Marquis of Wulin, Zi, was harsh and had lost the people's hearts; Ben was then supervising Dezhou and so linked several provinces' great houses in joint revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Ben and Shao went home to rebel; Inspector Zi of Wulin was harsh and had lost the people; Ben, supervising Dezhou, linked magnates of several provinces in revolt.

sentences.zh: 咨輸賄於賁，奔還廣州。

translations.literal: Zi paid bribes to Ben and fled back to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zi bribed Ben and fled to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 上遣咨與高州刺史孫冏、新州刺史盧子雄將兵擊之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Zi with Gaozhou inspector Sun Tong and Xinzhou inspector Lu Zixiong to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang emperor sent Zi with Sun Tong of Gaozhou and Lu Zixiong of Xinzhou against him.

sentences.zh: 咨，恢之子也。

translations.literal: Zi was Hui's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zi was Hui's son.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏又益新制十二條。

translations.literal: That year Western Wei again added twelve new articles.
translations.idiomatic: That year Western Wei added twelve new articles.

sentences.zh: 東魏丞相歡以諸州調絹不依舊式，民甚苦之，奏令悉以四十尺為匹。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan, because the provinces' silk levies did not follow the old measure, and the people suffered greatly, memorialized that all should use forty chi to the bolt.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan, because provincial silk levies ignored the old measure and the people suffered, ordered every bolt forty chi.

sentences.zh: 魏自喪亂以來，農商失業，六鎮之民相帥內徙，就食齊、晉，歡因之以成霸業。

translations.literal: Since the disorders Wei's farmers and merchants had lost their trades; the people of the six garrisons had led one another inward to seek food in Qi and Jin, and Huan had thereby achieved hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Since the disorders, farmers and merchants had failed; the six garrisons had moved inward to Qi and Jin for food, and Huan had built hegemony on them.

sentences.zh: 東西分裂，連年戰爭，河南州郡鞠為茂草，公私困竭，民多餓死。

translations.literal: East and west were split and warred year after year; Henan's provinces and commanderies were trampled to weeds; public and private were exhausted and many starved.
translations.idiomatic: East and west split and warred year on year; Henan's commanderies were weeds; public and private were drained and many starved.

sentences.zh: 歡命諸州濱河及津、梁皆置倉積穀以相轉漕，供軍旅，備饑饉，又於幽、瀛、滄、青四州傍海煮鹽。

translations.literal: Huan ordered all provinces along the river and at fords and bridges to set granaries and store grain for relay transport, to supply the army and guard against famine; he also had Yan, Ying, Cang, and Qing, the four provinces beside the sea, boil salt.
translations.idiomatic: Huan ordered river provinces and every ford and bridge to set granaries for relay grain for the army and famine; Yan, Ying, Cang, and Qing by the sea boiled salt.

sentences.zh: 軍國之費，粗得周贍。

translations.literal: Army and state expenses were roughly provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Army and state expenses were roughly met.

sentences.zh: 至是，東方連歲大稔，谷斛至九錢，山東之民稍復甦息矣。

translations.literal: By then the east had had great harvests several years running; grain was nine cash the hu, and the people of Shandong began to breathe again.
translations.idiomatic: By then the east had harvested several years; grain sold for nine cash the hu, and Shandong began to breathe again.

sentences.zh: 東魏尚書令高澄尚靜帝妹馮翊長公主，生子孝琬，朝貴賀之，澄曰：「此至尊之甥，先賀至尊。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Minister over the Masses Gao Cheng married the Quiet Emperor's younger sister, the Princess of Fengyi the Long; she bore son Xiaowan; the court nobles congratulated him, and Cheng said, "This is His Majesty's sister's child—congratulate His Majesty first.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng married the Quiet Emperor's sister, Princess of Fengyi the Long, and had Xiaowan; court nobles congratulated him. Cheng said, "This is the emperor's sister's child—congratulate the emperor first.

sentences.zh: 」三日，帝幸其第，賜錦彩布絹萬匹。

translations.literal: " Three days later the emperor visited his house and gave ten thousand bolts of brocade, silk, and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: " Three days later the emperor visited his house and gave ten thousand bolts of brocade, silk, and cloth.

sentences.zh: 於是諸貴競致禮遺，貨滿十室。

translations.literal: Thereupon the nobles vied to send gifts until ten rooms were full of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Then the nobles vied in gifts until ten rooms were piled with goods.

sentences.zh: 東魏臨淮王孝友表曰：「令制百家為族，二十五家為閭，五家為比。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Prince of Linhuai, Xiaoyou, memorialized, saying, "The present system makes a hundred households a clan, twenty-five a lane, and five a group.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiaoyou of Linhuai in Eastern Wei memorialized: "The present system makes a hundred households a clan, twenty-five a lane, five a group.

sentences.zh: 百家之內有帥二十五，征發皆免，苦樂不均，羊少狼多，復有蠶食，此之為弊久矣。

translations.literal: Within a hundred households there are twenty-five chiefs exempt from levies; joy and suffering are unequal—few sheep, many wolves, and again there is nibbling away; this harm has been long.
translations.idiomatic: Within a hundred households twenty-five chiefs are exempt from levies—joy and suffering unequal, few sheep and many wolves, and more nibbling away; the harm is old.

sentences.zh: 京邑諸坊，或七八百家唯一里正、二史，庶事無闕，而況外州乎！

translations.literal: In the capital wards, seven or eight hundred households sometimes have only one lane chief and two clerks, yet nothing is lacking in affairs—how much more in outer provinces!
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, seven or eight hundred households sometimes have only one lane chief and two clerks, yet nothing lacks—how much more in outer provinces!

sentences.zh: 請依舊置三正之名不改，而每閭止為二比，計族省十二丁，貲絹、番兵，所益甚多。

translations.literal: I beg to keep the old name of three chiefs unchanged but make each lane only two groups, reckoning twelve men saved per clan—silk levies and frontier duty would gain greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Keep the three chiefs' names but make each lane only two groups—twelve men saved per clan, with great gain in silk and frontier duty."

sentences.zh: 」事下尚書，寢不行。

translations.literal: " The matter went down to the Ministry of Works and slept without action.
translations.idiomatic: " It went to the Ministry of Works and slept.

sentences.zh: 安成望族劉敬躬以妖術惑眾，人多信之。

translations.literal: Liu Jinggong of the An Cheng great house bewitched the masses with sorcery; many believed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jinggong of the An Cheng magnates bewitched the people with sorcery; many believed.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝十四大同八年（

translations.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Wu, year 8 of the Datong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, eighth year of Datong (

sentences.zh: 壬戌，公元五四二年）

translations.literal: renxu, 542 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renxu, AD 542)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，敬躬據郡反，改元永漢，署官屬，進攻廬陵，逼豫章。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Jinggong held the commandery in rebellion, changed the era to Eternal Han, appointed officials, advanced on Luling, and pressed Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Jinggong rebelled in the commandery, styled his era Eternal Han, appointed officials, marched on Luling, and pressed Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 南方久不習兵，人情擾駭，豫章內史張綰募兵以拒之。

translations.literal: The south had long been unused to war; hearts were alarmed; Yuzhang interior minister Zhang Wan raised troops to resist.
translations.idiomatic: The south had long been unused to war; hearts quaked; Zhang Wan, interior minister of Yuzhang, raised troops to resist.

sentences.zh: 綰，纘之弟也。

translations.literal: Wan was Zuan's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wan was Zuan's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊戌，江州刺史湘東王繹遣司馬王僧辯、中兵曹子郢討敬躬，受綰節度。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuxu, Jiangzhou inspector Prince of Xiangdong, Yi, sent Mobile Headquarters Major Wang Sengbian and Central Troops Cao Ziyu to attack Jinggong, under Wan's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuxu, Prince Yi of Xiangdong, inspector of Jiangzhou, sent Wang Sengbian and Cao Ziyu against Jinggong under Wan's command.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊辰，擒敬躬，送建康，斬之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wuchen, Jinggong was captured, sent to Jiankang, and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wuchen, Jinggong was taken, sent to Jiankang, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 僧辯，神念之子也，該博辯捷，器宇肅然，雖射不穿札，而志氣高遠。

translations.literal: Sengbian was Shennian's son; he was broadly learned, quick in debate, and grave in bearing; though his archery did not pierce a leaf, his will was high and far.
translations.idiomatic: Sengbian was Shennian's son—learned, quick in debate, grave in bearing; though his arrow did not pierce a leaf, his will was high and far.

sentences.zh: 魏初置六軍。

translations.literal: Western Wei first established six armies.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei first established six armies.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙寅，東魏使兼散騎常侍李繪來聘。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on bingyin, Eastern Wei sent Associate Bearer of the Staff Li Hui on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on bingyin, Eastern Wei sent Li Hui as envoy.

sentences.zh: 繪，元忠之從子也。

translations.literal: Hui was Yuanzhong's younger cousin's son.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was grandson of Yuanzhong's younger cousin.

sentences.zh: 東魏丞相歡朝於鄴。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan attended court at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan attended court at Ye.

sentences.zh: 司徒孫騰坐事免；

translations.literal: Minister of Works Sun Teng was dismissed for an offense;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng, Minister of Works, was dismissed for an offense;

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以彭城王韶錄尚書事，侍中廣陽王湛為太尉，尚書右僕射高隆之為司徒。

translations.literal: on yiyou Prince Shao of Pengcheng was made to record affairs of the Masters of Writing, Palace Attendant Prince Zhan of Guangyang Grand Commandant, and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: on yiyou Prince Shao of Pengcheng recorded Masters of Writing affairs, Prince Zhan of Guangyang became Grand Commandant, and Gao Longzhi Right Vice Director became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 初，太傅尉景與丞相歡同歸爾朱榮，其妻，歡之姊也，自恃勳戚，貪縱不法，為有司所劾，繫獄；

translations.literal: At first Grand Tutor Wei Jing had returned with Chancellor Huan to Erzhu Rong; his wife was Huan's elder sister; relying on merit and kinship she was greedy and lawless and was impeached by the authorities and imprisoned;
translations.idiomatic: At first Wei Jing had returned with Gao Huan to Erzhu Rong; Jing's wife was Huan's elder sister; trusting merit and kinship she was greedy and lawless and was impeached and imprisoned;

sentences.zh: 歡三詣闕泣請，乃得免死。

translations.literal: Huan thrice went to the palace weeping to beg, and only then was death spared.
translations.idiomatic: Huan thrice went to the palace weeping to beg, and only then was death spared.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，降為驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: On dinghai he was reduced to Rapid Cavalry General with the Grandee title Opening the Mansion and Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai he was reduced to Rapid Cavalry General with Opening the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 歡往造之，景臥不起，大叫曰：「殺我時趣邪！

translations.literal: Huan went to visit him; Jing lay and would not rise, crying loudly, "When you killed me you were in a hurry, were you!
translations.idiomatic: Huan went to visit; Jing lay and would not rise, shouting, "When you killed me you were in a hurry, were you!

sentences.zh: 」歡撫而拜謝之。

translations.literal: " Huan stroked him and bowed in apology.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan stroked him and bowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以庫狄干為太傅，以領軍將軍婁昭為大司馬，封祖裔為尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: On xinmao Kudie Gan was made Grand Tutor, Army Supervisor Lou Zhao Grand Marshal, and Feng Zuyi Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Kudie Gan became Grand Tutor, Lou Zhao Army Supervisor became Grand Marshal, and Feng Zuyi became Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲辰，歡還晉陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiachen, Huan returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiachen, Gao Huan returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚戌，東魏以開府儀同三司、吏部尚書侯景為兼尚書僕射、河南道大行台，隨機防討。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on gengxu, Eastern Wei made Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes and Minister of Personnel Hou Jing concurrent Minister of Works and Grand Mobile Headquarters of Henan Route, to defend and strike as occasion required.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengxu, Eastern Wei made Hou Jing concurrent Minister of Works and Grand Mobile Headquarters of Henan Route, to defend and strike as occasion required.

sentences.zh: 魏以王盟為太保。

translations.literal: Western Wei made Wang Meng Grand Protector.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei made Wang Meng Grand Protector.

sentences.zh: 東魏丞相歡擊魏，入自汾、絳，連營四十里，丞相泰使王思政守玉壁以斷其道。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan attacked Wei, entering from Fen and Jiang, encamping in a line forty li long; Chancellor Tai sent Wang Sizheng to hold Yubi and cut his road.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan attacked Western Wei from Fen and Jiang, encamping forty li deep; Yuwen Tai sent Wang Sizheng to hold Yubi and block his road.

sentences.zh: 歡以書招思政曰：「若降，當授以并州。

translations.literal: Huan wrote to summon Sizheng, saying, "If you surrender, I will give you Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: Huan wrote Sizheng: "Surrender and I give you Bing."

sentences.zh: 」思政復書曰：「可朱渾道元降，何以不得？

translations.literal: " Sizheng replied, "Kezhun Hun Daoyuan surrendered—why did he not receive it?
translations.idiomatic: " Sizheng replied, "Kezhun Hun Daoyuan surrendered—why was he denied?

sentences.zh: 」冬，十月，己亥，歡圍玉壁，凡九日，遇大雪，士卒饑凍，多死者，遂解圍去。

translations.literal: " In winter, the tenth month, on jihai, Huan besieged Yubi nine days; heavy snow fell, soldiers hungered and froze, and many died; he then raised the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: " In winter, the tenth month, on jihai, Huan besieged Yubi nine days; snow fell, men starved and froze, and many died; he raised the siege and left.

sentences.zh: 魏遣太子欽鎮蒲板。

translations.literal: Western Wei sent the crown prince, Qin, to garrison Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei sent Crown Prince Qin to garrison Puban.

sentences.zh: 丞相泰出軍蒲板，至皁莢，聞歡退渡汾，追之不及。

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai led troops out from Puban to Zaojia; hearing Huan had crossed the Fen in retreat, he pursued but could not overtake.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai marched from Puban to Zaojia; hearing Huan had recrossed the Fen in retreat, he pursued but could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 十一月，東魏以可朱渾道元為并州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Eastern Wei made Kezhun Hun Daoyuan inspector of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Eastern Wei made Kezhun Hun Daoyuan inspector of Bing.

sentences.zh: 十二月，魏主狩於華陰，大享將士，丞相泰帥諸將朝之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Wei sovereign hunted at Huayin, feasted the officers and soldiers greatly, and Chancellor Tai led the generals to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, the Western Wei emperor hunted at Huayin and feasted the army; Yuwen Tai led the generals to attend.

sentences.zh: 起萬壽殿於沙苑北。

translations.literal: He raised Long Life Hall north of Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Long Life Hall north of Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，東魏遣兼散騎常侍楊斐來聘。

translations.literal: On xinhai Eastern Wei sent Associate Bearer of the Staff Yang Fei on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Eastern Wei sent Yang Fei as envoy.

sentences.zh: 孫冏、盧子雄討李賁，以春瘴方起，請待至秋；

translations.literal: Sun Tong and Lu Zixiong attacked Li Ben; because spring miasma was rising they asked to wait until autumn;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tong and Lu Zixiong attacked Li Ben; spring miasma was rising and they asked to wait until autumn;

sentences.zh: 廣州刺史新渝侯映不許，武林侯咨又趣之。

translations.literal: Guangzhou inspector Marquis of Xinyu, Ying, would not permit it, and Marquis of Wulin, Zi, pressed them on.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Ying of Xinyu would not allow it, and Zi of Wulin pressed them on.

sentences.zh: 冏等至合浦，死者什六七，眾潰而歸。

translations.literal: Tong and the rest reached Hepu; six or seven in ten died; the host broke and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Hepu; six or seven in ten died; the host broke and fled home.

sentences.zh: 映，憺之子也。

translations.literal: Ying was Dan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was Dan's son.

sentences.zh: 武林侯咨奏冏及子雄與賊交通，逗留不進，敕於廣州賜死。

translations.literal: Zi of Wulin memorialized that Tong and Zixiong had dealings with the bandits and lingered without advancing; an edict ordered them executed at Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zi memorialized that Tong and Zixiong trafficked with the rebels and lingered; an edict ordered them executed at Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子雄弟子略、子烈、主帥廣陵杜天合及弟僧明、新安周文育等帥子雄之眾攻廣州，欲殺映、咨，為子雄復冤。

translations.literal: Zixiong's younger brother's son Lue, son Lie, commander of Guangling Du Tianhe and younger brother Sengming, and Xin'an Zhou Wenyü led Zixiong's troops against Guangzhou, intending to kill Ying and Zi and avenge Zixiong.
translations.idiomatic: Lue and Lie, Zixiong's kin, with Du Tianhe of Guangling, his brother Sengming, and Zhou Wenyü of Xin'an led Zixiong's troops on Guangzhou to kill Ying and Zi and avenge him.

sentences.zh: 西江督護、高要太守吳興陳霸先帥精甲三千救之，大破子略等，殺天合，擒僧明、文育。

translations.literal: West River Protector and Gaoyao prefect Chen Baxian of Wuxing led three thousand picked armor to the rescue, routed Lue and the rest, killed Tianhe, and captured Sengming and Wenyü.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baxian of Wuxing, West River Protector and Gaoyao prefect, led three thousand picked men to the rescue, routed them, killed Tianhe, and took Sengming and Wenyü.

sentences.zh: 霸先以僧明、文育驍勇過人，釋之，以為主帥。

translations.literal: Baxian, because Sengming and Wenyü were surpassingly brave, released them and made them his commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Baxian, finding Sengming and Wenyü surpassingly brave, released them and made them his commanders.

sentences.zh: 詔以霸先為直閣將軍。

translations.literal: An edict made Baxian Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Baxian Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 魏丞相泰妻馮翊公主生子覺。

translations.literal: Western Wei Chancellor Tai's wife, the Princess of Fengyi, bore son Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai's wife, the Princess of Fengyi, bore Jue.

sentences.zh: 東魏以光州刺史李元忠為侍中。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei made Guangzhou inspector Li Yuanzhong Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei made Li Yuanzhong of Guangzhou Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 元忠雖處要任，不以物務干懷，唯飲酒自娛。

translations.literal: Though Yuanzhong held a weighty post, worldly affairs did not touch his mind; he drank for pleasure alone.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yuanzhong held a weighty post, worldly affairs did not touch him; he drank for pleasure alone.

sentences.zh: 丞相歡欲用為僕射，世子澄言其放達常醉，不可委以台閣。

translations.literal: Chancellor Huan wished to use him as Minister of Works; the heir Cheng said he was free and always drunk and could not be entrusted with the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan wished to make him Minister of Works; heir Cheng said he was free and always drunk and unfit for the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其子搔聞之，請節酒，元忠曰：「我言作僕射不勝飲酒樂，爾愛僕射，宜勿飲酒。

translations.literal: His son Sao heard of it and asked him to drink less; Yuanzhong said, "I say being Minister of Works is not as good as the joy of drinking—if you love the post of Minister of Works, you ought not to drink.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sao asked him to drink less; Yuanzhong said, "Being Minister of Works is not the joy of drinking—if you love that post, you ought not drink."

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝十四大同九年（

translations.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Wu, year 9 of the Datong era (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, ninth year of Datong (

sentences.zh: 癸亥，公元五四三年）

translations.literal: guihai, 543 CE)
translations.idiomatic: guihai, AD 543)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬戌，東魏大赦，改元武定。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renxu, Eastern Wei proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era to Martial Settlement.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renxu, Eastern Wei proclaimed amnesty and changed the era to Martial Settlement.

sentences.zh: 東魏御史中尉高仲密取吏部郎崔暹之妹，既而棄之，由是與暹有隙。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Imperial Censor Gao Zhongmi took the younger sister of Personnel Gentleman Cui Xuan, then cast her aside, and from this had a rift with Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhongmi, Eastern Wei Imperial Censor, married Cui Xuan of Personnel's sister, then cast her aside, and quarreled with Xuan.

sentences.zh: 仲密選用御史，多其親戚鄉黨，高澄奏令改選；

translations.literal: Zhongmi in selecting censors favored many of his kin and townsmen; Gao Cheng memorialized that the selection be changed;
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmi favored kin and townsmen in selecting censors; Gao Cheng had the list changed;

sentences.zh: 暹方為澄所寵任，仲密疑其構己，愈恨之。

translations.literal: Xuan was then Cheng's favorite; Zhongmi suspected he had framed him and hated him the more.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was Cheng's favorite; Zhongmi suspected a frame and hated him more.

sentences.zh: 仲密後妻李氏艷而慧，澄見而悅之，李氏不從，衣服皆裂，以告仲密，仲密益怨。

translations.literal: Zhongmi's later wife, the Li, was beautiful and clever; Cheng saw her and desired her; the Li would not yield and her clothes were all torn; she told Zhongmi and his hatred grew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmi's later wife Li was beautiful and clever; Cheng desired her; Li refused and her clothes were torn; she told Zhongmi and his hatred grew.

sentences.zh: 尋出為北豫州刺史，陰謀外叛。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as inspector of North Yuzhou and secretly plotted to rebel abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went out as inspector of North Yuzhou and secretly plotted defection.

sentences.zh: 丞相歡疑之，遣鎮城奚壽興典軍事，仲密但知民務。

translations.literal: Chancellor Huan suspected him and sent Xi Shouxing of the garrison city to handle military affairs; Zhongmi knew only civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan suspected him and sent Xi Shouxing to handle military affairs; Zhongmi handled only civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 仲密置酒延壽興，伏壯士，執之，二月，壬申，以虎牢叛，降魏。

translations.literal: Zhongmi set wine for Shouxing, hid strong men, and seized him; in the second month, on renshen, he rebelled at Tiger Mound and surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmi feasted Shouxing, hid strong men, and seized him; in the second month, on renshen, he rebelled at Tiger Mound and surrendered to Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 魏以仲密為侍中、司徒。

translations.literal: Western Wei made Zhongmi Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei made Zhongmi Palace Attendant and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 歡以仲密之叛由崔暹，將殺之，高澄匿暹，為之固請，歡曰：「我丐其命，須與苦手。

translations.literal: Huan, because Zhongmi's rebellion came from Cui Xuan, was about to kill Xuan; Gao Cheng hid Xuan and pleaded hard for him; Huan said, "I spare his life, but he must have a taste of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Huan blamed Cui Xuan for the revolt and was about to kill him; Gao Cheng hid Xuan and pleaded; Huan said, "I spare his life, but he must taste the staff.

sentences.zh: 」澄乃出暹，而謂大行台都官郎陳元康曰：「卿使崔暹得杖，勿復相見。

translations.literal: " Cheng then produced Xuan and told Grand Mobile Headquarters Director of Justice Chen Yuankang, "If you let Cui Xuan take the staff, see me no more.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng produced Xuan and told Chen Yuankang of Justice, "If Xuan takes the staff, see me no more.

sentences.zh: 」元康為之言於歡曰：「大王方以天下付大將軍，大將軍有一崔暹不能免其杖，父子尚爾，況於它人！

translations.literal: " Yuankang spoke to Huan for him, saying, "Your Highness is about to entrust the realm to the Grand General; the Grand General has one Cui Xuan and cannot spare him the staff—if father and son are thus, what of others!
translations.idiomatic: " Yuankang told Huan, "You entrust the realm to the Grand General; he has one Cui Xuan and cannot spare him the staff—if father and son are thus, what of others!

sentences.zh: 」歡乃釋之。

translations.literal: " Huan then released him.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan released him.

sentences.zh: 高季式在永安戍，仲密遣信報之；

translations.literal: Gao Jishi was garrisoning Yong'an; Zhongmi sent word to him;
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jishi garrisoned Yong'an; Zhongmi sent word;

sentences.zh: 季式走告歡，歡待之如舊。

translations.literal: Jishi ran to tell Huan, and Huan treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jishi ran to tell Huan, and Huan treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 魏丞相泰帥諸軍以應仲密，以太子少傅李遠為前驅，至洛陽，遣開府儀同三司於謹攻柏谷，拔之；

translations.literal: Western Wei Chancellor Tai led the armies to answer Zhongmi, with Crown Prince Tutor Li Yuan as vanguard; reaching Luoyang, he sent Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes Yu Jin to attack Cypress Valley and took it;
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai led the armies to answer Zhongmi with Li Yuan as vanguard; at Luoyang he sent Yu Jin to storm Cypress Valley and take it;

sentences.zh: 三月，壬申，圍河橋南城。

translations.literal: in the third month, on renshen, he besieged the south city at River Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: in the third month, on renshen, he besieged the south city at River Bridge.

sentences.zh: 東魏丞相歡將兵十萬至河北，泰退軍瀍上，縱火船於上流以燒河橋。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan led a hundred thousand men to the north of the river; Tai withdrew the army to the Yi bank and set fire ships upstream to burn the river bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan led a hundred thousand to the north bank; Tai withdrew to the Yi and sent fire ships upstream to burn the bridge.

sentences.zh: 斛律金使行台郎中張亮以小艇百餘載長鎖，伺火船將至，以釘釘之，引鎖向岸，橋遂獲全。

translations.literal: Hulü Jin had Mobile Headquarters Gentleman Zhang Liang take more than a hundred small boats loaded with long chains; when the fire ships were about to arrive he nailed them, drew the chains to shore, and the bridge was saved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Jin had Zhang Liang take a hundred small boats with long chains; when the fire ships came he nailed them, drew the chains ashore, and the bridge stood.

sentences.zh: 歡渡河，據邙山為陳，不進者數日。

translations.literal: Huan crossed the river, took Mount Mang for his battle line, and did not advance for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Huan crossed, formed line on Mount Mang, and did not advance for days.

sentences.zh: 泰留輜重於瀍曲，夜，登邙山以襲歡。

translations.literal: Tai left baggage at the Yi bend; at night he climbed Mount Mang to strike Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Tai left baggage at the Yi bend; at night he climbed Mount Mang to strike Huan.

sentences.zh: 候騎白歡曰：「賊距此四十餘里，蓐食乾飲而來。

translations.literal: Scouts told Huan, "Bandits are forty-odd li from here, eating dry rations on the march.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts told Huan, "The enemy is forty li off, eating dry on the march.

sentences.zh: 」歡曰：「自當渴死！

translations.literal: " Huan said, "They will die of thirst themselves!
translations.idiomatic: " Huan said, "They will die of thirst themselves!

sentences.zh: 」乃正陣以待之。

translations.literal: " He then set his ranks to wait.
translations.idiomatic: " He set ranks and waited.

sentences.zh: 戊申，黎明，泰軍與歡軍遇。

translations.literal: On wushen, at dawn, Tai's army and Huan's army met.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, at dawn, Tai's army met Huan's.

sentences.zh: 東魏彭樂以數千騎為右甄，沖魏軍之北垂，所向奔潰，遂馳入魏營。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei's Peng Yue led several thousand horse as the right wing, struck the northern flank of Wei's army, routed all before him, and galloped into the Wei camp.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Yue of Eastern Wei led several thousand horse on the right, shattered the northern flank, and galloped into the Wei camp.

sentences.zh: 人告彭樂叛，歡甚怒。

translations.literal: Men reported Peng Yue had rebelled; Huan was very angry.
translations.idiomatic: Men reported Peng Yue had turned; Huan raged.

sentences.zh: 俄而西北塵起，樂使來告捷，虜魏侍中、開府儀同三司、大都督臨洮王柬、蜀郡王榮宗、江夏王升、巨鹿王闡、譙郡王亮、詹事趙善及督將僚佐四十八人。

translations.literal: Soon dust rose in the northwest; Yue's messenger came to report victory, having captured Wei Palace Attendant, Bearer of the Staff Equal to the Three Dukes, Grand Commander Prince of Lintao, Dong, Prince of Shujun, Rongzong, Prince of Jiangxia, Sheng, Prince of Julu, Chan, Prince of Qiao, Liang, Grand Tutor Zhao Shan, and forty-eight officers and staff.
translations.idiomatic: Soon dust rose northwest; Yue's messenger reported victory—Palace Attendant Prince Dong of Lintao, Prince Rongzong of Shujun, Prince Sheng of Jiangxia, Prince Chan of Julu, Prince Liang of Qiao, Grand Tutor Zhao Shan, and forty-eight officers taken.

sentences.zh: 諸將乘勝擊魏，大破之，斬首三萬餘級。

translations.literal: The generals pressed the victory and struck Wei, routing them utterly and taking more than thirty thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: The generals pressed on and shattered Wei, taking more than thirty thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 歡使彭樂追泰，泰窘，謂樂曰：「汝非彭樂邪？

translations.literal: Huan sent Peng Yue to pursue Tai; Tai was hard pressed and said to Yue, "Are you not Peng Yue?
translations.idiomatic: Huan sent Peng Yue after Tai; Tai was cornered and said, "Are you not Peng Yue?

sentences.zh: 癡男子！

translations.literal: Fool of a man!
translations.idiomatic: Fool of a man!

sentences.zh: 今日無我，明日豈有汝邪！

translations.literal: Today without me, tomorrow will there be you?
translations.idiomatic: Today without me, tomorrow will there be you?

sentences.zh: 何不急還營，收汝金寶！

translations.literal: Why not hurry back to camp and gather your gold and gems!
translations.idiomatic: Why not hurry back and gather your gold and gems!

sentences.zh: 」樂從其言，獲泰金帶一囊以歸，言於歡曰：「黑獺漏刃，破膽矣！

translations.literal: " Yue followed his words, took a pouch of Tai's gold belt, and returned, telling Huan, "The Black Badger slipped the blade—his courage is broken!
translations.idiomatic: " Yue obeyed, took Tai's gold belt, and told Huan, "The Black Badger slipped the blade—his courage is broken!

sentences.zh: 」歡雖喜其勝而怒其失泰，令伏諸地，親捽其頭，連頓之，並數以沙苑之敗，舉刃將下者三，噤齘良久。

translations.literal: " Huan was glad of the victory but angry he had lost Tai; he had Yue lie on the ground, seized his head himself, and knocked it again and again, also reckoning up the defeat at Shayuan; thrice he raised the blade to strike and held his teeth a long while.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan was glad of victory but furious Tai escaped; he had Yue lie down, seized his head and knocked it again and again, reckoning Shayuan; thrice he raised the blade and gnashed long.

sentences.zh: 樂曰：「乞五千騎，復為王取之。

translations.literal: Yue said, "I beg five thousand horse to take him again for my lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Give me five thousand horse and I will take him again."

sentences.zh: 」歡曰：「汝縱之何意？

translations.literal: " Huan said, "Why did you let him go?
translations.idiomatic: " Huan said, "Why did you let him go?

sentences.zh: 而言復取邪！

translations.literal: And speak of taking him again!
translations.idiomatic: And speak of taking him again!

sentences.zh: 」命取絹三千匹壓樂背，因以賜之。

translations.literal: " He ordered three thousand bolts of silk piled on Yue's back and then gave them to him.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered three thousand bolts of silk piled on Yue's back, then gave them to him.

sentences.zh: 明日，復戰，泰為中軍，中山公趙貴為左軍，領軍若干惠等為右軍。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again; Tai was center army, Duke of Zhongshan Zhao Gui left army, and Army Supervisor Ruogan Hui and others right army.
translations.idiomatic: Next day they fought again; Tai held center, Zhao Gui of Zhongshan the left, Ruogan Hui and others the right.

sentences.zh: 中軍、右軍合擊東魏，大破之，悉俘其步卒。

translations.literal: Center and right together struck Eastern Wei, routed them utterly, and took all their foot soldiers prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Center and right together shattered Eastern Wei and took every foot soldier.

sentences.zh: 歡失馬，赫連陽順下馬以授歡。

translations.literal: Huan lost his horse; Helian Yangshun dismounted and gave his horse to Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Huan lost his horse; Helian Yangshun dismounted and gave him his.

sentences.zh: 歡上馬走，從者步騎七人，追兵至，親信都督尉興慶曰：「王速去，興慶腰有百箭，足殺百人。

translations.literal: Huan mounted and fled; seven foot and horse followed; pursuers came up; trusted commander Wei Xingqing said, "My lord, go quickly—Xingqing has a hundred arrows at his belt, enough to kill a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Huan mounted and fled with seven men; pursuers closed; Wei Xingqing said, "My lord, go—I have a hundred arrows, enough for a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 」歡曰：「事濟，以爾為懷州刺史；

translations.literal: " Huan said, "If the affair succeeds, I make you inspector of Hua;
translations.idiomatic: " Huan said, "If we win, you are inspector of Hua;

sentences.zh: 若死，用爾子！

translations.literal: if I die, I use your son!
translations.idiomatic: if I die, I use your son!

sentences.zh: 」興慶曰：「兒小，願用兄！

translations.literal: " Xingqing said, "My son is small—I wish to use my elder brother!
translations.idiomatic: " Xingqing said, "My son is small—use my brother!

sentences.zh: 」歡許之。

translations.literal: " Huan consented.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan consented.

sentences.zh: 興慶拒戰，矢盡而死。

translations.literal: Xingqing held them off until his arrows were spent and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xingqing held them until his arrows were spent and died.

sentences.zh: 東魏軍士有逃奔魏者，告以歡所在，泰募勇敢三千人，皆執短兵，配大都督賀拔勝以攻之。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei soldiers who fled to Wei reported where Huan was; Tai recruited three thousand brave men, all with short weapons, and gave them to Grand Commander Heba Sheng to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei deserters told where Huan was; Tai took three thousand brave men with short weapons under Heba Sheng.

sentences.zh: 勝識歡於行間，執槊與十三騎逐之，馳數里，槊刃垂及，因字之曰：「賀六渾，賀拔破胡必殺汝！

translations.literal: Sheng knew Huan in the ranks, took his spear with thirteen riders and chased him several li; the spear point nearly reached him, and he called by his style, "He Liu Hun, Heba Pohu will surely kill you!
translations.idiomatic: Sheng knew Huan in the ranks, took his spear with thirteen riders and chased him; the point nearly reached him; he called, "He Liu Hun, Heba Pohu will kill you!

sentences.zh: 」歡氣殆絕，河州刺史劉洪徽從傍射勝，中其二騎，武衛將軍段韶射勝馬，斃之。

translations.literal: " Huan nearly lost breath; Hezhou inspector Liu Honghui shot from the side and hit two of his riders; Palace Guard General Duan Shao shot Sheng's horse and killed it.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan nearly fainted; Liu Honghui of Hezhou shot from the side and dropped two riders; Duan Shao of the Palace Guard shot Sheng's horse dead.

sentences.zh: 比副馬至，歡已逸去。

translations.literal: By the time the spare horse came, Huan had already escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Before the spare horse came, Huan was gone.

sentences.zh: 勝歎曰：「今日不執弓矢，天也！

translations.literal: Sheng sighed, "Today I did not carry bow and arrows—Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sighed, "Today I carried no bow—Heaven!

sentences.zh: 魏南郢州刺史耿令貴，大呼，獨入敵中，鋒刃亂下，人皆謂已死，俄奮刀而還。

translations.literal: Western Wei's Nanying inspector Geng Linggui shouted and entered the enemy alone; blades fell on every side and all thought him dead, but presently he flourished his sword and came back.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Linggui, inspector of Nanying in Western Wei, shouted and entered the enemy alone; blades fell everywhere and all thought him dead; then he flourished his sword and came back.

sentences.zh: 如是數四，當令貴前者死傷相繼。

translations.literal: He did this four times; those before Linggui died and were wounded in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He did this four times; those before him fell in heaps.

sentences.zh: 乃謂左右曰：「吾豈樂殺人！

translations.literal: He then told those at his side, "Do I delight in killing!
translations.idiomatic: He told his men, "Do I delight in killing!

sentences.zh: 壯士除賊，不得不爾。

translations.literal: A stalwart rids the realm of bandits—he cannot do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: A stalwart rids bandits—he cannot do otherwise.

sentences.zh: 若不能殺賊，又不為賊所傷，何異逐坐人也！

translations.literal: If he cannot kill bandits and is not wounded by bandits, how is he different from one who chases a seat!
translations.idiomatic: If he neither kills bandits nor is wounded by them, how is he different from one chasing a seat!

sentences.zh: 左軍趙貴等五將戰不利，東魏兵復振。

translations.literal: Left army Zhao Gui and five other generals fought ill; Eastern Wei troops rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gui and five generals on the left fought ill; Eastern Wei rallied.

sentences.zh: 泰與戰，又不利。

translations.literal: Tai fought again and again without success.
translations.idiomatic: Tai fought again without success.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，魏兵遂遁，東魏兵追之；

translations.literal: It happened to be evening; Wei troops then fled and Eastern Wei pursued;
translations.idiomatic: Evening came; Wei fled and Eastern Wei pursued.

sentences.zh: 獨孤信、於謹收散卒自後擊之，追兵驚擾，魏諸軍由是得全。

translations.literal: Dugu Xin and Yu Jin gathered scattered soldiers and struck from behind; the pursuers were alarmed and thrown into confusion, and by this all Wei armies were saved whole.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Xin and Yu Jin gathered the scattered and struck from behind; pursuers panicked, and every Wei army got clear.

sentences.zh: 若於惠夜引去，東魏兵追之；

translations.literal: Ruogan Hui led away by night; Eastern Wei pursued;
translations.idiomatic: Ruogan Hui marched off by night; Eastern Wei pursued.

sentences.zh: 惠徐下馬，顧命廚人營食，食畢，謂左右曰：「長安死，此中死，有以異乎？

translations.literal: Hui slowly dismounted, ordered the cook to prepare food, and when the meal was done told those at his side, "To die in Chang'an or to die here—how are they different?
translations.idiomatic: Hui slowly dismounted, had the cook prepare food, and when it was done said, "Die in Chang'an or die here—what difference?

sentences.zh: 」乃建旗鳴角，收散卒徐還；

translations.literal: " He then raised banners and sounded horns, gathered scattered soldiers, and returned at leisure;
translations.idiomatic: " He raised banners, sounded horns, gathered the scattered, and returned at leisure;

sentences.zh: 追騎疑有伏兵，不敢逼。

translations.literal: The pursuers suspected an ambush and did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuers suspected an ambush and did not dare press close.

sentences.zh: 泰遂入關，屯渭上。

translations.literal: Tai then entered the pass and encamped on the Wei north bank.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai then entered the pass and encamped on the north bank of the Wei.

sentences.zh: 歡進至陝，泰使開府儀同三司達奚武等拒之。

translations.literal: Huan advanced to Shaan; Tai sent Kaifu Yitong Sansi Daxi Wu and others to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan advanced to Shaan; Yuwen Tai sent Daxi Wu and others to block him.

sentences.zh: 行台郎中封子繪言於歡曰：「混壹東西，正在今日。

translations.literal: Mobile Headquarters Director Feng Zihui said to Huan, "To unify east and west—today is the day.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zihui of the mobile headquarters said to Huan, "To unify east and west—the moment is today.

sentences.zh: 昔魏太祖平漢中，不乘勝取巴、蜀，失在遲疑，後悔無及。

translations.literal: In old times Emperor Taizu of Wei pacified Hanzhong but did not press the victory to take Ba and Shu; the loss lay in hesitation, and regret came too late.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Emperor Taizu of Wei took Hanzhong but did not follow up to seize Ba and Shu; hesitation cost him, and he regretted it ever after.

sentences.zh: 願大王不以為疑。

translations.literal: I beg Your Highness not to regard it with suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you, my lord, not to doubt it.

sentences.zh: 」歡深然之，集諸將議進止，鹹以為「野無青草，人馬疲瘦，不可遠追。

translations.literal: " Huan deeply agreed, gathered his generals to discuss advancing or halting, and all held that with no fresh grass in the fields and men and horses worn thin, they could not pursue far.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was deeply persuaded, called his generals to debate whether to advance, and all said, "There is no fresh grass in the fields; men and horses are exhausted—they cannot be chased far."

sentences.zh: 」陳元康曰：「兩雄交爭，歲月已久。

translations.literal: " Chen Yuankang said, "Two great rivals have contended for years.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuankang said, "Two great rivals have contended for years.

sentences.zh: 今幸而大捷，天授我也，時不可失，當乘勝追之。

translations.literal: Now, by good fortune, we have won a great victory—Heaven has granted it to us; the moment must not be lost; we should press the victory while pursuit is still possible.
translations.idiomatic: Now, by good fortune, we have won a great victory—Heaven has granted it to us. The moment must not be lost; we should press the victory while pursuit is still possible."

sentences.zh: 」歡曰：「若遇伏兵，孤何以濟？

translations.literal: " Huan said, "If we meet an ambush, how shall I escape?
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "If we meet an ambush, how shall I escape?"

sentences.zh: 」元康曰：「王前沙苑失利，彼尚無伏；

translations.literal: " Yuankang said, "When Your Highness lost at Shaxi, they still set no ambush;
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang said, "When Your Highness lost at Shaxi, they still set no ambush;

sentences.zh: 今奔敗若此，何能遠謀！

translations.literal: now they flee in defeat like this—how could they plan far ahead!
translations.idiomatic: now they flee in defeat like this—how could they plan far ahead!

sentences.zh: 若捨而不追，必成後患。

translations.literal: If you abandon pursuit, you will surely breed future trouble.
translations.idiomatic: If you abandon pursuit, you will surely breed future trouble."

sentences.zh: 」歡不從，使劉豐生將數千騎追泰，遂東歸。

translations.literal: " Huan did not follow the advice. He sent Liu Fengsheng with several thousand horse in pursuit of Tai, then turned east and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Huan did not follow the advice. He sent Liu Fengsheng with several thousand horse in pursuit of Tai, then turned east and returned.

sentences.zh: 泰召王思政於玉壁，將使鎮虎牢，未至而泰敗，乃使守恆農。

translations.literal: Tai summoned Wang Sizheng from Yubi, intending to station him at Hulao; before Sizheng arrived Tai was defeated, so he was sent to hold Hengnong instead.
translations.idiomatic: Tai summoned Wang Sizheng from Yubi, intending to station him at Hulao; before Sizheng arrived Tai was defeated, so he was sent to hold Hengnong instead.

sentences.zh: 思政入城，令開門解衣而臥，慰勉將士，示不足畏。

translations.literal: Sizheng entered the city, ordered the gates opened, stripped to his shirt, and lay down, encouraging the troops and showing he had nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng entered the city, ordered the gates opened, stripped to his shirt, and lay down—encouraging the troops and showing he had nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 後數日，劉豐生至城下，憚之，不敢進，引軍還。

translations.literal: Several days later Liu Fengsheng reached the foot of the walls; he feared Sizheng, dared not advance, and withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Liu Fengsheng reached the foot of the walls; he feared Sizheng, dared not advance, and withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 思政乃修城郭，起樓櫓，營農田，積芻粟，由是恆農始有守禦之備。

translations.literal: Sizheng then repaired the walls, raised towers and parapets, opened fields for garrison farming, and stored fodder and grain—whereby Hengnong first gained means of defense.
translations.idiomatic: Sizheng then repaired the walls, raised towers and parapets, opened fields for garrison farming, and stored fodder and grain—whereby Hengnong first gained real means of defense.

sentences.zh: 丞相泰求自貶，魏主不許。

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai asked to be demoted; the Wei sovereign would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Tai asked to be demoted; the Wei sovereign would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 是役也，魏諸將皆無功，唯耿令貴與太子武衛率王胡仁、都督王文達力戰功多。

translations.literal: In this campaign the Wei generals all won no merit; only Geng Linggui, Crown Prince Martial Guard Commandant Wang Huren, and Supervisor Wang Wenda fought hard and achieved much.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign the Wei generals all won no merit; only Geng Linggui, Crown Prince Martial Guard Commandant Wang Huren, and Supervisor Wang Wenda fought hard and achieved much.

sentences.zh: 泰欲以雍、岐、北雍三州授之，以州有優劣，使探籌取之。

translations.literal: Tai wished to grant them Yong, Qi, and Northern Yong provinces; because the provinces differed in quality, he had them draw lots to choose.
translations.idiomatic: Tai wished to grant them Yong, Qi, and Northern Yong provinces; because the provinces differed in quality, he had them draw lots to choose.

sentences.zh: 仍賜胡仁名勇，令貴名豪，文達名信，用彰其功。

translations.literal: He also bestowed on Huren the name Yong, on Linggui the name Hao, and on Wenda the name Xin, to make their merit manifest.
translations.idiomatic: He also bestowed on Huren the name Yong, on Linggui the name Hao, and on Wenda the name Xin, to make their merit manifest.

sentences.zh: 於是廣募關、隴豪右以增軍旅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he widely recruited powerful families of Guan and Long to enlarge the army.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he widely recruited powerful families of Guan and Long to enlarge the army.

sentences.zh: 高仲密之將叛也，陰遣人扇動冀州豪傑，使為內應，東魏遣高隆之馳驛慰撫，由是得安。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi was about to rebel, he secretly sent men to stir the powerful families of Jizhou to act as inner supporters; Eastern Wei sent Gao Longzhi post-haste by relay to comfort and pacify them, and thus the region was kept quiet.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi was about to rebel, he secretly sent men to stir the powerful families of Jizhou to act as inner supporters; Eastern Wei sent Gao Longzhi post-haste by relay to comfort and pacify them, and thus the region was kept quiet.

sentences.zh: 高澄密書與隆之曰：「仲密枝黨與之俱西者，宜悉收其家屬，以懲將來。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng sent a secret letter to Longzhi saying, "Of Zhongmi's branch and party who went west with him, you should seize all their families to warn those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng sent a secret letter to Longzhi saying, "Of Zhongmi's branch and party who went west with him, you should seize all their families to warn those who come after."

sentences.zh: 」隆之以為恩旨既行，理無追改，若復收治，示民不信，脫致驚擾，所虧不細，乃啟丞相歡而罷之。

translations.literal: " Longzhi held that since the grace-edict had already been issued, it was unreasonable to reverse it; if they seized and punished them again it would show the people the court did not keep faith, and should alarm and disturbance arise the loss would not be slight—he memorialized Chancellor Huan and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi held that since the grace-edict had already been issued, it was unreasonable to reverse it; if they seized and punished them again it would show the people the court did not keep faith, and should alarm and disturbance arise the loss would not be slight—he memorialized Chancellor Huan and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 以太子詹事謝舉為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Household Aide Xie Ju was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Household Aide Xie Ju was made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，林邑王攻李賁，賁將范修破林邑於九德。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the king of Linyi attacked Li Ben; Ben's general Fan Xiu defeated Linyi at Jiude.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the king of Linyi attacked Li Ben; Ben's general Fan Xiu defeated Linyi at Jiude.

sentences.zh: 清水氐酋李鼠仁，乘魏之敗，據險作亂；

translations.literal: Li Shuren, Di chieftain of Qingshui, took advantage of Wei's defeat to seize the passes and rise in rebellion;
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuren, Di chieftain of Qingshui, took advantage of Wei's defeat to seize the passes and rise in rebellion;

sentences.zh: 隴右大都督獨孤信屢遣軍擊之，不克。

translations.literal: Grand Commander of the Right Dugu Xin repeatedly sent troops to strike him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commander of the Right Dugu Xin repeatedly sent troops to strike him but could not overcome him.

sentences.zh: 丞相泰遣典簽天水趙昶往諭之，諸酋長聚議，或從或否；

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai sent Registry Clerk Zhao Chang of Tianshui to instruct them; the chieftains gathered to deliberate, some assenting and some refusing;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Tai sent Registry Clerk Zhao Chang of Tianshui to instruct them; the chieftains gathered to deliberate, some assenting and some refusing;

sentences.zh: 其不從者欲加刃於昶，昶神色自若，辭氣逾厲，鼠仁感悟，遂相帥降。

translations.literal: those who refused wished to set blades to Chang, but Chang's expression stayed calm and his words grew ever sterner; Shuren was moved to understanding, and they thereupon led one another in submission.
translations.idiomatic: those who refused wished to set blades to Chang, but Chang's expression stayed calm and his words grew ever sterner; Shuren was moved to understanding, and they thereupon led one another in submission.

sentences.zh: 氐酋梁道顯叛，泰復遣昶諭降之，徙其豪帥四十餘人並部落於華州，泰即以昶為都督，使領之。

translations.literal: The Di chieftain Liang Daoxian rebelled; Tai again sent Chang to instruct him to submit, moved more than forty of their powerful chiefs together with their tribes to Huazhou, and made Chang colonel to command them.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Liang Daoxian rebelled; Tai again sent Chang to instruct him to submit, moved more than forty of their powerful chiefs together with their tribes to Huazhou, and made Chang colonel to command them.

sentences.zh: 泰使諜潛入虎牢，令守將魏光固守。

translations.literal: Tai sent a spy secretly into Hulao and ordered the defending general Wei Guang to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Tai sent a spy secretly into Hulao and ordered the defending general Wei Guang to hold firm.

sentences.zh: 侯景獲之，改其書云：「宜速去。

translations.literal: Hou Jing captured him and altered the letter to read, "You should leave at once.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing captured him and altered the letter to read, "You should leave at once."

sentences.zh: 」縱諜入城，光宵遁。

translations.literal: " He released the spy into the city; Guang fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: He released the spy into the city; Guang fled by night.

sentences.zh: 景獲高仲密妻子送鄴，北豫、洛二州復入於東魏。

translations.literal: Jing seized Gao Zhongmi's wife and children and sent them to Ye; Northern Yu and Luo provinces again fell to Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Jing seized Gao Zhongmi's wife and children and sent them to Ye; Northern Yu and Luo provinces again fell to Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬辰，東魏以克復虎牢，降死罪已下囚，唯不赦高仲密家。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renchen, Eastern Wei, for recovering Hulao, reduced the punishment of prisoners down to capital crimes, pardoning all below that rank, but did not pardon Zhongmi's household alone.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renchen, Eastern Wei, for recovering Hulao, reduced the punishment of prisoners down to capital crimes, pardoning all below that rank, but did not pardon Zhongmi's household alone.

sentences.zh: 丞相歡以高乾有義勳，高昂死王事，季式先自告，皆為之請，免其從坐。

translations.literal: Chancellor Huan, because Gao Gan had merit of righteousness, Gao Ang died in the king's service, and Jishi had reported himself first, all pleaded on their behalf and exempted them from joint punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Huan, because Gao Gan had merit of righteousness, Gao Ang died in the king's service, and Jishi had reported himself first, all pleaded on their behalf and exempted them from joint punishment.

sentences.zh: 仲密妻李氏當死，高澄盛服見之，曰：「今日何如？

translations.literal: Zhongmi's wife Lady Li was due for execution; Gao Cheng came to see her in full dress and said, "How is it today?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmi's wife Lady Li was due for execution; Gao Cheng came to see her in full dress and said, "How is it today?"

sentences.zh: 」李氏默然，遂納之。

translations.literal: " Lady Li was silent; he thereupon took her in.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was silent; he thereupon took her in.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以侯景為司空。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Hou Jing was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Hou Jing was made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏大赦。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wei proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 以王盟為太傅，廣平王贊為司空。

translations.literal: Wang Meng was made Grand Tutor and the Prince of Guangping, Zan, Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng was made Grand Tutor and the Prince of Guangping, Zan, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙丑，東魏以汾州刺史斛律金為大司馬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yichou, Eastern Wei made Fenzhou inspector Helü Jin Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yichou, Eastern Wei made Fenzhou inspector Helü Jin Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 東魏遣兼散騎常侍李渾等來聘。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei sent Acting Palace Attendant Li Hun and others on a friendly embassy.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei sent Acting Palace Attendant Li Hun and others on a friendly embassy.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，甲午，東魏主狩於西山；

translations.literal: In winter, the eleventh month, on jiawu, the Eastern Wei ruler hunted on Western Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the eleventh month, on jiawu, the Eastern Wei ruler hunted on Western Mountain;

sentences.zh: 乙巳，還宮。

translations.literal: on yisi he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: on yisi he returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 高澄啟解侍中，東魏主以其弟并州刺史太原公洋代之。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng memorialized to resign as Palace Attendant; the Eastern Wei ruler had his younger brother, Bingzhou inspector the Duke of Taiyuan, Yang, replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng memorialized to resign as Palace Attendant; the Eastern Wei ruler had his younger brother, Bingzhou inspector the Duke of Taiyuan, Yang, replace him.

sentences.zh: 丞相歡築長城於肆州北山，西自馬陵，東至土□登，四十日罷。

translations.literal: Chancellor Huan built a long wall on the northern mountains of Sizhou, west from Maling east to Tudeng, finishing in forty days.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Huan built a long wall on the northern mountains of Sizhou, west from Maling east to Tudeng, finishing in forty days.

sentences.zh: 魏諸牧守共謁丞相泰，泰命河北太守裴俠別立，謂諸牧守曰：「裴俠清慎奉公，為天下最。

translations.literal: The Wei prefects and governors all came to call on Chancellor Tai; Tai ordered Hebei prefect Pei Xia to stand apart and said to the prefects and governors, "Pei Xia is pure, cautious, and serves the public—he is the finest under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei prefects and governors all came to call on Chancellor Tai; Tai ordered Hebei prefect Pei Xia to stand apart and said to the prefects and governors, "Pei Xia is pure, cautious, and serves the public—he is the finest under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 有如俠者，可與俱立！

translations.literal: If any are like Xia, you may stand with him!
translations.idiomatic: If any are like Xia, you may stand with him!"

sentences.zh: 」眾默然，無敢應者。

translations.literal: " All were silent; none dared answer.
translations.idiomatic: All were silent; none dared answer.

sentences.zh: 泰乃厚賜俠，朝野歎服，號為「獨立君」。

translations.literal: Tai then richly rewarded Xia; court and countryside admired him and called him "the Stand-Alone Lord."
translations.idiomatic: Tai then richly rewarded Xia; court and countryside admired him and called him "the Stand-Alone Lord."

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝十四大同十年（

translations.literal: Great Ancestor Emperor Wu, fourteenth year of Datong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang, fourteenth year of Datong (

sentences.zh: 甲子，公元五四四年）

translations.literal: jiazi, 544 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiazi, AD 544)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，李賁自稱越帝，置百官，改元天德。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Li Ben styled himself Emperor of Yue, set up the hundred offices, and changed the era name to Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Li Ben styled himself Emperor of Yue, set up the hundred offices, and changed the era name to Tiande.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸巳，東魏丞相歡巡行冀、定二州，校河北戶口損益，因朝於鄴。

translations.literal: In the third month, on guisi, Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan toured Jizhou and Dingzhou, checked the gain and loss of household registers north of the Yellow River, and on that account attended court at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guisi, Eastern Wei Chancellor Huan toured Jizhou and Dingzhou, checked the gain and loss of household registers north of the Yellow River, and on that account attended court at Ye.

sentences.zh: 甲午，上幸蘭陵，謁建寧陵，使太子入守宮城；

translations.literal: On jiawu the emperor visited Lanling, paid respects at Jianning Mausoleum, and had the crown prince enter to guard the palace;
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the emperor visited Lanling, paid respects at Jianning Mausoleum, and had the crown prince enter to guard the palace;

sentences.zh: 辛丑，謁脩陵。

translations.literal: on xinchou he paid respects at Xiuling.
translations.idiomatic: on xinchou he paid respects at Xiuling.

sentences.zh: 丙午，東魏以開府儀同三司孫騰為太保。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Eastern Wei made Palace Gate General of the First Rank Sun Teng Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Eastern Wei made Palace Gate General of the First Rank Sun Teng Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 己酉，上幸京口城北固樓，更名北顧；

translations.literal: On jiyou the emperor visited the Beigu Tower north of Jingkou and renamed it North Gaze;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou the emperor visited the Beigu Tower north of Jingkou and renamed it North Gaze;

sentences.zh: 庚戌，幸回賓亭，宴鄉里故老及所經近縣迎候者，少長數千人，各賚錢二千。

translations.literal: on gengxu he visited Huibin Pavilion, feasted the elders of his native place and those from nearby counties who had come to welcome him—young and old numbering several thousand—and gave each two thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: on gengxu he visited Huibin Pavilion, feasted the elders of his native place and those from nearby counties who had come to welcome him—young and old numbering several thousand—and gave each two thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 壬子，東魏以高澄為大將軍、領中書監，元弼為錄尚書事，左僕射司馬子如為尚書令，侍中高洋為左僕射。

translations.literal: On renzi, Eastern Wei made Gao Cheng Grand General and Director of the Masters of Writing, Yuan Bi Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Left Vice Director Sima Ziru Director of the Masters of Writing, and Palace Attendant Gao Yang Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Eastern Wei made Gao Cheng Grand General and Director of the Masters of Writing, Yuan Bi Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing, Left Vice Director Sima Ziru Director of the Masters of Writing, and Palace Attendant Gao Yang Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 丞相歡多在晉陽，孫騰、司馬子如、高岳、高隆之，皆歡之親舊，委以朝政，鄴中謂之四貴，其權勢熏灼中外，率多專恣驕貪。

translations.literal: Chancellor Huan was often at Jinyang; Sun Teng, Sima Ziru, Gao Yue, and Gao Longzhi were all Huan's intimates, entrusted with court government—Ye called them the Four Dignitaries; their power scorched within and without, and for the most part they were willful, arrogant, and greedy.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Huan was often at Jinyang; Sun Teng, Sima Ziru, Gao Yue, and Gao Longzhi were all Huan's intimates, entrusted with court government—Ye called them the Four Dignitaries; their power scorched within and without, and for the most part they were willful, arrogant, and greedy.

sentences.zh: 歡欲損奪其權，故以澄為大將軍、領中書監，移門下機事總歸中書，文武賞罰皆稟於澄。

translations.literal: Huan wished to curtail their power, and therefore made Cheng Grand General and Director of the Masters of Writing, shifting the Secretariat's business in total to the Masters of Writing; civil and military rewards and punishments all were reported to Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huan wished to curtail their power, and therefore made Cheng Grand General and Director of the Masters of Writing, shifting the Secretariat's business in total to the Masters of Writing; civil and military rewards and punishments all were reported to Cheng.

sentences.zh: 孫騰見澄，不肯盡敬，澄叱左右牽下於床，築以刀環，立之門外。

translations.literal: When Sun Teng saw Cheng he would not show full respect; Cheng shouted for attendants to drag him down from the couch, beat him with sword rings, and set him standing outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Teng saw Cheng he would not show full respect; Cheng shouted for attendants to drag him down from the couch, beat him with sword rings, and set him standing outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 太原公洋於澄前拜高隆之，呼為叔父，澄怒罵之。

translations.literal: The Duke of Taiyuan, Yang, bowed to Gao Longzhi before Cheng and called him uncle; Cheng cursed him in anger.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Taiyuan, Yang, bowed to Gao Longzhi before Cheng and called him uncle; Cheng cursed him in anger.

sentences.zh: 歡謂群公曰：「兒子浸長，公宜避之。

translations.literal: Huan told the assembled lords, "Sons grow daily; you lords ought to give way.
translations.idiomatic: Huan told the assembled lords, "Sons grow daily; you lords ought to give way."

sentences.zh: 」於是公卿以下，見澄無不聳懼。

translations.literal: " Thereupon from the dukes and ministers downward, all who saw Cheng did so in dread.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon from the dukes and ministers downward, all who saw Cheng did so in dread.

sentences.zh: 庫狄干，澄姑之婿也，自定州來謁，立於門外，三日乃得見。

translations.literal: Kudi Gan, Cheng's aunt's son-in-law, came from Dingzhou to call; he stood outside the gate three days before he was received.
translations.idiomatic: Kudi Gan, Cheng's aunt's son-in-law, came from Dingzhou to call; he stood outside the gate three days before he was received.

sentences.zh: 澄欲置腹心於東魏主左右，擢中兵參軍崔季舒為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Cheng wished to place trusted men at the Eastern Wei ruler's side and promoted Central Army Staff Member Cui Jishu to Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng wished to place trusted men at the Eastern Wei ruler's side and promoted Central Army Staff Member Cui Jishu to Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 澄每進書於帝，有所諫請，或文辭繁雜，季舒輒修飾通之。

translations.literal: Whenever Cheng forwarded a memorial to the emperor with remonstrance or request, if the wording was tangled Jishu would revise and make it clear.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Cheng forwarded a memorial to the emperor with remonstrance or request, if the wording was tangled Jishu would revise and make it clear.

sentences.zh: 帝報澄父子之語，常與季舒論之，曰：「崔中書，我乳母也。

translations.literal: The emperor, in reporting Cheng and his father's words, often discussed them with Jishu and said, "Director Cui is my wet nurse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in reporting Cheng and his father's words, often discussed them with Jishu and said, "Director Cui is my wet nurse."

sentences.zh: 」季舒，挺之從子也。

translations.literal: " Jishu was a nephew of Cui Ting's.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu was a nephew of Cui Ting's.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，乙卯，上還自蘭陵。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on yimao, the emperor returned from Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on yimao, the emperor returned from Lanling.

sentences.zh: 五月，甲申朔，魏丞相泰朝於長安。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the new moon of jiashen, Wei Chancellor Tai attended court at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the new moon of jiashen, Wei Chancellor Tai attended court at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 甲午，東魏遣散騎常侍魏季景來聘。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Eastern Wei sent Palace Attendant Wei Jijing on a friendly embassy.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Eastern Wei sent Palace Attendant Wei Jijing on a friendly embassy.

sentences.zh: 季景，收之族叔也。

translations.literal: Jijing was a clansman of Wei Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Jijing was a clansman of Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 尚書令何敬容妾弟盜官米，以書屬領軍河東王譽；

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing He Jingrong's younger brother by a concubine stole official grain and used a letter to ask Military Supervisor Prince Yu of Hedong for favor;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing He Jingrong's younger brother by a concubine stole official grain and used a letter to ask Military Supervisor Prince Yu of Hedong for favor;

sentences.zh: 丁酉，敬容坐免官。

translations.literal: on dingyou Jingrong was removed from office for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: on dingyou Jingrong was removed from office for the crime.

sentences.zh: 東魏廣陽王湛卒。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei Prince Zhan of Guangyang died.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei Prince Zhan of Guangyang died.

sentences.zh: 魏琅邪貞獻公賀拔勝諸子在東者，丞相歡盡殺之，勝憤恨發疾而卒。

translations.literal: The sons of Wei Duke of Langye, the Loyal and Offering Helüba Sheng, who were in the east, Chancellor Huan killed them all; Sheng died of rage and illness.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Wei Duke of Langye, the Loyal and Offering Helüba Sheng, who were in the east, Chancellor Huan killed them all; Sheng died of rage and illness.

sentences.zh: 丞相泰常謂人曰：「諸將對敵神色皆動，唯賀拔公臨陳如平時，真大勇也！

translations.literal: Chancellor Tai often told others, "When the generals face the enemy their expressions all change; only Duke Helüba at battle is as at ordinary times—true great courage!
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Tai often told others, "When the generals face the enemy their expressions all change; only Duke Helüba at battle is as at ordinary times—true great courage!"

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，魏更權衡度量，命尚書蘇綽損益三十六條之制，總為五卷，頒行之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wei revised weights and measures, ordered Master of Writing Su Chuo to revise the thirty-six-article code for gain and loss, compiled it in five scrolls in all, and promulgated it.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Wei revised weights and measures, ordered Master of Writing Su Chuo to revise the thirty-six-article code for gain and loss, compiled it in five scrolls in all, and promulgated it.

sentences.zh: 搜簡賢才為牧守令長，皆依新制而遣焉。

translations.literal: He searched out the worthy to be prefects, governors, and magistrates, and dispatched them all according to the new code.
translations.idiomatic: He searched out the worthy to be prefects, governors, and magistrates, and dispatched them all according to the new code.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，百姓便之。

translations.literal: Within several years the common people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Within several years the common people found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 魏自正光以後，政刑弛縱，在位多貪污。

translations.literal: From Zhenguang onward Wei government and punishments had grown lax; those in office were mostly corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhenguang onward Wei government and punishments had grown lax; those in office were mostly corrupt.

sentences.zh: 丞相歡啟以司州中從事宋游道為御史中尉，澄固請以吏部郎崔暹為之，以游道為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Chancellor Huan memorialized to make Song Youdao of Sizhou Central Army Attendant Censor-in-Chief; Cheng firmly asked that Ministry of Personnel Attendant Cui Xuan be made to the post, with Youdao as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Huan memorialized to make Song Youdao of Sizhou Central Army Attendant Censor-in-Chief; Cheng firmly asked that Ministry of Personnel Attendant Cui Xuan be made to the post, with Youdao as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 澄謂暹、游道曰：「卿一人處南台，一人處北省，當使天下肅然。

translations.literal: Cheng told Xuan and Youdao, "You, one at the Southern Terrace and one at the Northern Bureau, should make all under Heaven stand in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng told Xuan and Youdao, "You, one at the Southern Terrace and one at the Northern Bureau, should make all under Heaven stand in awe."

sentences.zh: 」暹選畢義雲等為御史，時稱得人。

translations.literal: " Xuan chose Bi Yiyun and others as censors; the age called it obtaining the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan chose Bi Yiyun and others as censors; the age called it obtaining the right men.

sentences.zh: 義雲，眾敬之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yiyun was a great-grandson of Bi Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyun was a great-grandson of Bi Zhongjing.

sentences.zh: 澄欲假暹威勢，諸公在坐，令暹後至，通名，高視徐步，兩人挈裾而入；

translations.literal: Cheng wished to borrow Xuan's awesomeness; when the lords were seated he had Xuan arrive last, announce his name, walk in with high gaze and slow step, two men lifting his robe;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng wished to borrow Xuan's awesomeness; when the lords were seated he had Xuan arrive last, announce his name, walk in with high gaze and slow step, two men lifting his robe;

sentences.zh: 澄分庭對揖，暹不讓而坐，觴再行，即辭去。

translations.literal: Cheng met him with equal bows across the courtyard; Xuan did not yield but sat, and after two rounds of wine at once took leave.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng met him with equal bows across the courtyard; Xuan did not yield but sat, and after two rounds of wine at once took leave.

sentences.zh: 澄留之食，暹曰：「適受敕在台檢校。

translations.literal: Cheng kept him to eat; Xuan said, "I have just received orders to inspect at the Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng kept him to eat; Xuan said, "I have just received orders to inspect at the Terrace."

sentences.zh: 」遂不待食而去，澄降階送之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon left without waiting for the meal; Cheng descended the steps to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon left without waiting for the meal; Cheng descended the steps to see him off.

sentences.zh: 它日，澄與諸公出，之東山，遇暹於道，前驅為赤棒所擊，澄回馬避之。

translations.literal: Another day Cheng went out with the lords to Eastern Mountain and met Xuan on the road; the outriders were struck by red staffs and Cheng turned his horse aside.
translations.idiomatic: Another day Cheng went out with the lords to Eastern Mountain and met Xuan on the road; the outriders were struck by red staffs and Cheng turned his horse aside.

sentences.zh: 尚書令司馬子如以丞相歡故人，當重任，意氣自高，與太師咸陽王坦貪黷無厭；

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Sima Ziru, as Chancellor Huan's old friend, held heavy responsibility and was proud in spirit; he and Grand Master Prince Tan of Xianyang were insatiably greedy;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Sima Ziru, as Chancellor Huan's old friend, held heavy responsibility and was proud in spirit; he and Grand Master Prince Tan of Xianyang were insatiably greedy;

sentences.zh: 暹前後彈子如、坦及并州刺史可朱渾道元等罪狀，無不極筆。

translations.literal: Xuan impeached Ziru, Tan, and Bingzhou inspector Kezhunhun Daoyuan and others for crimes, in every case to the full limit of the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan impeached Ziru, Tan, and Bingzhou inspector Kezhunhun Daoyuan and others for crimes, in every case to the full limit of the brush.

sentences.zh: 宋游道亦劾子如、坦及太保孫騰、司徒高隆之、司空侯景、尚書元羨等。

translations.literal: Song Youdao also impeached Ziru, Tan, and Grand Guardian Sun Teng, Minister of Works Gao Longzhi, Minister of Works Hou Jing, and Master of Writing Yuan Xian and others.
translations.idiomatic: Song Youdao also impeached Ziru, Tan, and Grand Guardian Sun Teng, Minister of Works Gao Longzhi, Minister of Works Hou Jing, and Master of Writing Yuan Xian and others.

sentences.zh: 澄收子如繫獄，一宿，發盡白，辭曰：「司馬子如從夏州策杖投相王，王給露車一乘，豢牸牛犢，犢在道死，唯豢角存，此外皆取之於人。

translations.literal: Cheng seized Ziru and imprisoned him; in one night his hair turned entirely white. His statement read, "Sima Ziru came from Xiazhou leaning on a staff to join the Prince-Regent; the Prince gave one covered cart, a cow and calf for rearing—the calf died on the road and only the horns of the rearing cow remain; beyond that everything was taken from others.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng seized Ziru and imprisoned him; in one night his hair turned entirely white. His statement read, "Sima Ziru came from Xiazhou leaning on a staff to join the Prince-Regent; the Prince gave one covered cart, a cow and calf for rearing—the calf died on the road and only the horns of the rearing cow remain; beyond that everything was taken from others."

sentences.zh: 」丞相歡以書敕澄曰：「司馬令，吾之故舊，汝宜寬之。

translations.literal: " Chancellor Huan sent a letter commanding Cheng, "Director Sima is my old friend; you should treat him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Huan sent a letter commanding Cheng, "Director Sima is my old friend; you should treat him leniently."

sentences.zh: 」澄駐馬行街，出子如，脫其鎖；

translations.literal: " Cheng halted his horse in the street, released Ziru, and removed his fetters;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng halted his horse in the street, released Ziru, and removed his fetters;

sentences.zh: 子如懼曰：「非作事邪？

translations.literal: Ziru said in fear, "This is not a capital case?
translations.idiomatic: Ziru said in fear, "This is not a capital case?"

sentences.zh: 」八月，癸酉，削子如官爵。

translations.literal: " In the eighth month, on guiyou, Ziru's office and rank were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on guiyou, Ziru's office and rank were stripped.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲申，以濟陰王暉業為太尉；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jiashen, Prince Ye of Jiyin was made Grand Commandant;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiashen, Prince Ye of Jiyin was made Grand Commandant;

sentences.zh: 太師咸陽王坦以王還第，元羨等皆免官，其餘死黜者甚眾。

translations.literal: Grand Master Prince Tan of Xianyang was returned to his estate as a prince; Yuan Xian and others were all removed from office, and of the rest many were executed or dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master Prince Tan of Xianyang was returned to his estate as a prince; Yuan Xian and others were all removed from office, and of the rest many were executed or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 久之，歡見子如，哀其憔悴，以膝承其首，親為擇虱，賜酒百瓶，羊五百口，米五百石。

translations.literal: After a long while Huan saw Ziru, pitied his haggard look, supported his head on his knee, personally picked lice for him, and gave a hundred jars of wine, five hundred sheep, and five hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while Huan saw Ziru, pitied his haggard look, supported his head on his knee, personally picked lice for him, and gave a hundred jars of wine, five hundred sheep, and five hundred piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 高澄對諸貴極言褒美崔暹，且戒屬之。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng spoke to the dignitaries at length in praise of Cui Xuan and also warned them to heed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng spoke to the dignitaries at length in praise of Cui Xuan and also warned them to heed him.

sentences.zh: 丞相歡書與鄴下諸貴曰：「崔暹居憲台，咸陽王、司馬令皆吾布衣之舊，尊貴親暱，無過二人，同時獲罪，吾不能救，諸君其慎之！

translations.literal: Chancellor Huan wrote to the dignitaries at Ye, "Cui Xuan holds the Censorate; Prince Tan of Xianyang and Director Sima are both my old companions in plain cloth—none more honored or intimate than those two—yet both fell into crime at once and I could not save them; you lords, take care!
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Huan wrote to the dignitaries at Ye, "Cui Xuan holds the Censorate; Prince Tan of Xianyang and Director Sima are both my old companions in plain cloth—none more honored or intimate than those two—yet both fell into crime at once and I could not save them; you lords, take care!"

sentences.zh: 宋游道奏駁尚書違失數百條，省中豪吏王儒之徒並鞭斥之，令、僕已下皆側目。

translations.literal: Song Youdao memorialized to refute several hundred errors of the Masters of Writing; the powerful clerks Wang Ru and others in the bureau were all flogged and driven out, and from directors and vice directors downward all looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: Song Youdao memorialized to refute several hundred errors of the Masters of Writing; the powerful clerks Wang Ru and others in the bureau were all flogged and driven out, and from directors and vice directors downward all looked askance.

sentences.zh: 高隆之誣游道有不臣之言，罪當死。

translations.literal: Gao Longzhi slandered Youdao with words of disloyalty; the crime merited death.
